brief_summary: This experimental study uses a Single-Case Experimental Design (SCED) with multiple baselines across participants to evaluate the impact of a non motorized assistive device (DAP) on muscle effort in care givers during their professional activities. Each participant completes a 12-day protocol consisting of three phases (A1 - B - A2), with the initial baseline (A1, no device) randomized between 2 and 6 days, followed by a 6-day intervention phase (B, wearing the non-motorized DAP), and a final withdrawal phase (A2, no device) adjusted to complete the 12-day period. Muscle effort is continuously quantified as a percentage of maximum voluntary contraction using mechanomyographic sensors (MOTEN Technologies) placed on the lumbar and biceps muscles, as well as the quadriceps at the Fondation Saint-Hélier site.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Maximum Voluntary Contraction (% MVC) of target muscle groups
title: The Impact of Using a Non-motorised Physical Assistance Device on the Prevention of Musculoskeletal Disorders Amongst Care-givers

brief_summary:
Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) is a bacterium that infects the stomach and may cause gastritis, peptic ulcer disease, and dyspeptic symptoms. Although antibiotic-based treatments are commonly used to eradicate the infection, treatment failure remains a clinical concern.

This randomized controlled trial evaluated whether adding N-acetylcysteine (NAC) or curcumin to standard treatment could improve H. pylori eradication and reduce dyspeptic symptoms.

A total of 150 adults with H. pylori infection were assigned to one of three groups: standard treatment alone, standard treatment plus NAC, or standard treatment plus curcumin. Standard treatment consisted of esomeprazole, amoxicillin, levofloxacin, and bismuth for 14 days.

The primary outcome was H. pylori eradication, assessed using a 13C-urea breath test four weeks after treatment completion. Secondary outcomes included changes in dyspeptic symptoms measured using the Short-Form Leeds Dyspepsia Questionnaire (SF-LDQ) and the occurrence of adverse effects.
primary_outcomes: Helicobacter pylori Eradication Rate
title: Effects of Adjunctive N-Acetylcysteine and Curcumin on Helicobacter Pylori Eradication and Dyspeptic Symptoms: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if the SHE-OUD program helps women who are receiving buprenorphine treatment for opioid use disorder (OUD), have experienced sexual violence, and have PTSD. The study will examine whether the program is practical to deliver, safe, and acceptable to participants. The main questions it aims to answer are: Is SHE-OUD feasible, acceptable, and satisfying for women in OUD treatment who have experienced sexual violence and have PTSD? Does SHE-OUD increase participants' engagement in mental health treatment for PTSD? The study will first evaluate SHE-OUD in a small open trial, then compare SHE-OUD to a control condition in a randomized trial to see if SHE-OUD increases engagement in mental health treatment. Participants will: complete the SHE-OUD program (or, in the randomized trial, either SHE-OUD or the control condition), continue regular buprenorphine treatment for OUD, complete assessments at the start of the study and at a 1-month follow-up, and answer questions about mental health, treatment engagement, and satisfaction with the program.
primary_outcomes: Mental Health Treatment Initiation
Mental Health Treatment Utilization
title: Addressing Violence in the Context of Opioid Use Disorder Care

brief_summary:
Spanish multicenter registry of cardioneuroablation (ablation of cardiac ganglionated plexi) in patients with reflex syncope and functional bradyarrhythmias Background Cardioneuroablation (CNA) is the catheter ablation of the ganglionated plexi (GP) of the intrinsic cardiac autonomic nervous system, located in the atrial epicardial fat, to reduce parasympathetic tone on the sinus node and the atrioventricular (AV) node. It has been proposed as an alternative to pacemaker implantation in patients, often young, with cardioinhibitory reflex syncope or vagally mediated bradyarrhythmias. However, the available evidence comes mainly from single-center series at highly experienced centers, with heterogeneous techniques (choice of atrium, number of GP targeted, localization method, type of anesthesia) and no standardized acute procedural endpoint. Data from real-world clinical practice are needed to define its efficacy and safety, and to identify which patients and which procedural strategies are associated with better outcomes.

Objectives Primary: to assess syncope recurrence after CNA in real-world clinical practice in Spain.

Secondary: 1) to describe the procedural characteristics and complications of CNA; 2) to identify clinical and procedural predictors of success; 3) to evaluate the change in syncope and presyncope burden and the need for pacemaker implantation during follow-up.

Design Observational, multicenter, ambispective, ongoing registry with 27 participating hospitals in Spain. Cases performed since June 2018 are collected retrospectively, and prospective enrollment of consecutive patients has been in place since April 2021.

Study population

Inclusion criteria: consecutive patients undergoing CNA for syncope with one of the following phenotypes:

* Cardioinhibitory reflex syncope: bradycardia \<40 bpm or asystole documented on tilt testing, Holter monitoring or implantable loop recorder.
* Mixed reflex syncope: blood pressure drop preceding the heart rate drop on tilt testing.
* Functional sinus node dysfunction.
* Functional AV block. Procedure

CNA is performed according to the usual practice of each center. The operator chooses:

* the approach (right atrium, left atrium or both);
* the number of GP targeted;
* the GP localization method (anatomical, fragmented electrograms, high-frequency stimulation, extracardiac vagal stimulation or combinations);
* the type of anesthesia (general anesthesia, deep sedation, conscious sedation). Data collected
* Baseline: demographics, body mass index, cardiovascular history and structural heart disease, type of syncope, number of syncopal and presyncopal episodes before CNA, and diagnostic tests (tilt testing, Holter, implantable loop recorder, atropine test).
* Procedural: approach, GP targeted, localization method, type of anesthesia, ablation catheter and navigation system, RF power and number of applications, procedure and fluoroscopy times, heart rate before and after CNA and response to atropine after the procedure.
* Safety: procedure-related complications, including sinus node dysfunction, inappropriate sinus tachycardia and vascular complications.
* Follow-up: syncope and presyncope recurrence, number of episodes per year, need for pacemaker implantation and other clinical events.

Endpoints Primary endpoint: first syncope recurrence after CNA. Secondary endpoints: procedure-related complications; number of syncopal and presyncopal episodes per year before and after CNA; pacemaker implantation during follow-up.

Ongoing sub-studies:

1. long-term follow-up of these patients and identification of predictors of recurrence;
2. redo procedures, in patients requiring more than one CNA;
3. patients followed with an implantable loop recorder (subcutaneous Holter). Expected relevance This registry will provide multicenter real-world data on CNA in Spain. It will help to identify the patients most likely to benefit from the procedure and the technical aspects associated with success, and will generate hypotheses for future randomized trials.
primary_outcomes: syncope
title: Spanish Registry of Cardioneuroablation

brief_summary:
Obesity is a complex, multifactorial disease driven by metabolic dysfunction, chronic low-grade inflammation, oxidative stress, and gut microbiota dysbiosis. The pathogenesis of obesity is closely linked to white adipose tissue (WAT) dysfunction, particularly the dysregulation of lipogenic and adipogenic pathways, leading to adipocyte hypertrophy and ectopic fat deposition. Although sleeve gastrectomy is a gold-standard intervention for severe obesity, a subset of patients experiences suboptimal long-term weight loss and cardiometabolic improvements, potentially due to persistent inflammation and metabolic resistance.

The gut-adipose axis has emerged as a critical therapeutic target. Modulation of the gut microbiome through synbiotic supplementation may alleviate metabolic endotoxemia and systemic inflammation, thereby improving energy homeostasis. However, the impact of presurgical synbiotic intervention on adipose tissue remodeling in patients undergoing sleeve gastrectomy remains largely unexplored.

This triple-blind, randomized controlled trial (RCT) aims to evaluate the efficacy of synbiotic supplementation in obese women candidates for sleeve gastrectomy. The objective is to investigate the effect of synbiotics on the expression of key lipogenic and adipogenic transcriptional factors (e.g., SREBP-1c, C/EBPα, PPARγ, LXRs) and rate-limiting enzymes (e.g, FAS, ACC) in white adipose tissue.

The study hypothesis is that presurgical synbiotic intervention will modulate adipose tissue function, thereby enhancing postoperative weight loss and improving metabolic profiles. The study aims to provide evidence for a potential therapeutic strategy to optimize clinical outcomes in bariatric patients by targeting the molecular mechanisms underlying adipose tissue expansion.
primary_outcomes: Fatty Acid Synthase (FAS) mRNA level and protein level in subcutaneous and abdominal adipose tissue
Sterol Regulatory Element-Binding Protein-1c (SREBP) mRNA and protein levels in abdominal and subcutaneous adipose tissue
Acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC) mRNA and protein levels in subcutaneous and abdominal adipose tissue
Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPAR-γ ) mRNA level in abdominal and subcutaneous adipose tissue
Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ coactivator 1-α (PGC-1α) mRNA level in abdominal and subcutaneous adipose tissue
C/EBP-alpha (CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein alpha) mRNA level in abdominal and subcutaneous adipose tissue
LXRα (Liver X Receptor alpha) mRNA levels in abdominal and subcutaneous adipose tissues
title: Effects of Synbiotic Supplementation on Adipose Tissue Factors in Obese Women Undergoing Sleeve Gastrectomy

brief_summary: The GABAPLAST study explores how commonly prescribed GABAergic drugs prescribed during post-stroke rehabilitation affect cortical plasticity and motor learning capacity. Using a multiple-baseline single-case design, the study evaluates the effects of Baclofen, Oxazepam, and Gabapentin in subacute stroke patients according to their clinical indication. Cortical plasticity capacity is measured with transcranial magnetic stimulation and Paired Associative Stimulation (TMS/PAS). The study aims to determine whether these drugs interfere with or preserve brain plasticity during recovery.
primary_outcomes: Brain plasticity
title: Effect of GABAergic Treatments on Cortical Plasticity and Motor Learning Capacity in the Subacute Phase After Stroke

brief_summary:
Efficacy and Mechanisms of Time-Domain Interferential Transcranial Electrical Stimulation in Treating Depression Associated with Childhood Trauma Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a prevalent mental illness characterized by high suicide rates and substantial social burden. According to the World Health Organization's (WHO) Global Health Assessment Report on Depression, the global prevalence of MDD reached 350 million cases in 2021, making it the second leading cause of death among individuals aged 15-29 years. MDD is defined by core symptoms of persistent low mood and anhedonia, often accompanied by cognitive, behavioral, and physiological disturbances. These symptoms significantly impair individuals' daily functioning, social interactions, and occupational performance, and some patients may even engage in self-harm or suicidal behaviors\[1,2\]. MDD imposes a heavy burden on global disease burden, as well as on affected individuals, their families, and society at large.

Existing studies have identified childhood trauma as a major risk factor for MDD. Epidemiological research indicates that individuals who experience childhood trauma face a higher risk of developing MDD, anxiety disorders, or comorbid conditions. Childhood trauma may account for 28.9% of all mental disorders, exerting a lifelong impact on physical and mental health. Notably, 45.59% of MDD patients have a history of at least one type of childhood trauma. Adults with a history of childhood trauma are 2.66-3.73 times more likely to develop MDD compared to those without such experiences.

Animal studies suggest that environmental stress can induce depression-like behaviors in adolescent female rats, accompanied by elevated levels of corticosterone (CORT) and cholecystokinin (CCK), as well as reduced neuropeptide Y (NPY) expression\[3,4,5,6\]. However, there are currently no effective and safe pharmacological treatments for childhood trauma in clinical practice, and the overall quality of existing evidence remains low. While psychological interventions have been shown to reduce depressive symptoms in MDD patients with childhood trauma, the supporting evidence from evidence-based medicine is insufficient. Therefore, effective, non-pharmacological, well-tolerated, and accessible treatment modalities are crucial for managing MDD complicated by childhood trauma. Research has explored the underlying physiological mechanisms of childhood trauma from perspectives including neuroendocrinology, neuroinflammation, and neuroimaging, but a clear and comprehensive explanation remains elusive.

Temporal interference (TI) electrical stimulation is an emerging non-invasive brain stimulation technique. It utilizes two high-frequency carrier waves to generate low-frequency envelope oscillations in deep brain regions, enabling precise targeted modulation of subcortical structures such as the basal ganglia. Preliminary studies have demonstrated the potential clinical efficacy of TI in treating depression and trauma-related disorders. This paper reviews the research progress and future prospects of TI electrical stimulation in the management of MDD with childhood trauma.
primary_outcomes: Change in depression severity measured by the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17)
title: Efficacy and Mechanisms of Time-Domain Interferential Transcranial Electrical Stimulation in Treating Depression Associated With Childhood Trauma

The purpose of this study is to evaluate the effect of animation-supported breastfeeding education given to primiparous pregnant women on prenatal breastfeeding self-efficacy and infant feeding intentions.

Breastfeeding is vital for both maternal and infant health; however, primiparous women often face challenges due to lack of experience, low confidence, and inadequate knowledge. This study hypothesizes that visually engaging, animation-supported education will significantly increase prenatal breastfeeding self-efficacy and strengthen positive infant feeding intentions compared to standard prenatal care.

Participants will be randomly allocated to either an intervention group receiving animation-supported breastfeeding education or a control group receiving routine care. Outcomes will be evaluated using standardized assessment scales before and after the intervention.
primary_outcomes: Prenatal Breastfeeding Self-Efficacy Scale (PBSES) Score
Infant Feeding Intentions (IFI) Scale Score

brief_summary: Biliary atresia (BA) is a severe infantile cholangiopathy characterized by progressive inflammation and fibrotic obliteration of the intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts. Although Kasai portoenterostomy can restore bile drainage, more than 50% of affected infants still progress to end-stage liver disease and require liver transplantation. BA is not merely a structural biliary obstruction but a complex liver disease involving cholestasis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, lipid peroxidation, bile acid metabolic disorders, and collagen deposition. Current clinical assessment relies mainly on serum liver function tests and semi-quantitative histological scoring, which cannot reveal the overall metabolic landscape or spatial heterogeneity of the liver. Raman imaging is a label-free, high-spatial-resolution molecular vibrational imaging technique that can simultaneously detect lipids, proteins, nucleic acids, glycogen, collagen, bilirubin, bile acids, and oxidative stress products. It has demonstrated metabolic phenotyping capability in tumor heterogeneity, organ development, and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease. However, the in situ spatial distribution of metabolites in BA liver-especially metabolic differences among portal, parenchymal, and centrilobular regions, the metabolic microenvironment around bile duct reaction foci, and metabolic boundaries of fibrous septa-remains unexplored by conventional metabolomics. Preliminary studies by our group have identified collagen deposition, oxidative stress, and bile acid metabolic abnormalities in BA liver. We hypothesize that BA liver undergoes coordinated metabolic reprogramming that forms characteristic Raman-capturable metabolic signatures, which may serve as novel tools for disease stratification and prognosis prediction. This study aims to construct a Raman-based liver metabolic atlas and evaluate its prognostic value.
primary_outcomes: Juandice clearance
title: Construction of a Liver Metabolic Atlas in Biliary Atresia Based on Raman Spectroscopic Imaging

brief_summary:
After shoulder replacement surgery, surgeons send questionnaires to their patients to learn how they are doing (pain, shoulder function, satisfaction). Many patients do not answer. This study tests the best way to obtain these answers.

The study is nested in a multicenter study of pain after shoulder arthroplasty conducted in four French centers (host study RetroPAinRSACAll, supported by Ramsay Santé). The clinical results of the host study are not the subject of this registration: this study evaluates only the method used to collect the information.

All patients first receive an email invitation (when an email address is available) and, the next day, a text message (SMS) with a personal link to the questionnaire and a phone number to answer at any time by talking with an automated voice assistant. Patients who have not answered two days after the first contact are randomly assigned to one of two follow-up strategies: (1) further digital reminders (SMS on day 3 and day 5, email on day 7), or (2) up to three phone calls from a conversational artificial intelligence (AI) voice agent on days 3, 5 and 7, which asks the same questions orally. In both groups, patients can answer at any time online or by calling the voice assistant, and contacts stop as soon as the questionnaire is completed or the patient refuses.

The main outcome is the proportion of patients who complete the questionnaire within 14 days of the first contact.
lead_sponsor: Institut de Chirurgie Reparatrice Locomoteur et Sports
primary_outcomes: Questionnaire Completion by Day 14 Among Randomized Participants
title: AI Voice Calls Versus Text and Email Reminders for Questionnaire Response After Shoulder Arthroplasty

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial tests whether listening to an audio hypnotherapy recording before a planned cesarean section reduces preoperative anxiety and changes blood markers of inflammation. brief_summary: This study evaluates the efficacy and safety of adding olmesartan to sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) therapy in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and persistent albuminuria. Participants receive olmesartan at a dose of either 20 mg or 40 mg daily in addition to their ongoing SGLT2i treatment. Changes in urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), renal function, and blood pressure are assessed over a 9-month follow-up period. The study aims to evaluate the potential additional renoprotective effects of olmesartan in patients with type 2 diabetes who continue to have albuminuria despite SGLT2i therapy.

brief_summary:
Children born with esophageal atresia need surgery shortly after birth. For many years, the standard operation was a thoracotomy, an opening in the chest that can sometimes lead to changes in the shape of the chest wall. Although these changes are visible on X rays, doctors still do not fully understand how much they affect breathing later in childhood. A newer, less invasive technique called thoracoscopy uses small incisions and appears to cause fewer chest deformities, but its impact on lung function has not yet been clearly established.

This study aims to compare the breathing capacity of children aged 6 to 9 who were operated on using either thoracotomy or thoracoscopy. The main question is whether one group is more likely to develop restrictive lung syndrome, a condition in which the lungs cannot expand normally. To answer this, the study relies on lung function tests and chest X rays performed during routine follow up visits.

Beyond this primary goal, the study also examines other possible breathing problems, the presence of chest wall abnormalities, and factors that might influence lung health, such as nutrition, physical activity, associated malformations, and overall quality of life.

A total of at least 360 children across France will participate. They are identified through national registries and invited during scheduled follow up consultations.
primary_outcomes: to assess the presence of a restrictive lung syndrome in patients with type 3 esophageal atresia (EA) depending on the type of surgical approach used (conventional or minimally invasive).
title: Respiratory Restriction Leaded by Conventional or Minimally Invasive Sugical Repair of Oesophageal Atresia in Children

brief_summary: In this study, the effect-implementation mixed research design was adopted. The patients were assigned to the intervention group and the control group at a ratio of 2 : 1 by the central stratified randomization method. The stratification factors were four phenotypes of psychosomatic symptoms ( anxiety and depression, sleep disorders, fatigue and mixed symptoms ). The intervention group was determined by the three-stage conversation model of doctor-patient joint decision-making, and the personalized acupuncture intervention program was determined. Combined with the patient 's own needs and service accessibility, the hospital intervention subgroup or the medical-social-home intervention subgroup scenario was determined. The control group was given routine nursing. Because the intervention requires informed interaction between doctors and patients, only outcome evaluators and data analysts are blinded. The intervention period was 8 weeks of treatment and 4 weeks of follow-up, a total of 12 weeks. Based on the evaluation of the effect of acupuncture intervention on the improvement of psychosomatic symptoms, the study was guided by the CFIR framework to evaluate the implementation of the hospital intervention subgroup and the medical-social-family intervention subgroup formed after the joint decision-making of doctors and patients, identify the implementation obstacles and promotion factors, and evaluate the implementation outcomes such as acceptability, feasibility, implementation loyalty and coverage.
lead_sponsor: First Teaching Hospital of Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine
primary_outcomes: Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Breast, FACT-B
title: Study on the Construction and Implementation Effect of a Traditional Chinese Medicine-Based Mental-Physical Comorbidity Linked Health-Management System of "Hospital-Community-Family" for Breast Cancer Patients

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to find out whether a therapy called Narrative Exposure Therapy (NET) is suitable and could be helpful for people who:

* have experienced trauma
* find it hard to manage their emotions
* have a history of violent offending

NET is already used in clinical practice, but there is limited research about how helpful it is for this group. This study will look at whether NET:

* is feasible to use in this population
* reduces symptoms of post-traumatic stress (such as nightmares, flashbacks, and feeling on edge)
* helps people manage their emotions better What is NET? NET is a one-to-one talking therapy for people who have experienced trauma. In NET, the patient and the therapist create a timeline of your life. This includes both positive experiences and difficult or traumatic events. individuals then talk through the traumatic events in a safe and structured way, with support from the therapist.

The aim is to help the brain process these memories so they cause less distress in everyday life. NET focuses on you as a whole person, not just on your offending history.
primary_outcomes: International Trauma Questionnaire
title: Using Narrative Exposure Therapy to Treat Violent Offenders With Post Traumatic Stress and Emotion Dysregulation.

brief_summary:
This study aimed to evaluate the effects of stress management training on subjective happiness and perceived stress levels in older adults.

Stress can negatively affect the psychological well-being and quality of life of older adults. Stress management training may help older adults develop effective coping strategies, reduce perceived stress, and improve subjective happiness.

The study included an intervention group that received a four-week stress management training program and a control group that did not receive the training. The program included information about stress and its effects, relaxation techniques, deep breathing exercises, cognitive-behavioral strategies, and mindfulness practices.

Participants' subjective happiness and perceived stress levels were assessed before and after the intervention using the Subjective Happiness Scale and the Perceived Stress Scale.

The study aimed to determine whether stress management training could improve subjective happiness and reduce perceived stress among older adults.
primary_outcomes: Change in Subjective Happiness Scale Score
Change in Perceived Stress Scale-14 Score
title: Effect of Stress Management Training on Happiness and Perceived Stress in Older Adults

brief_summary: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a rare and progressive disease associated with significant illness and reduced survival. The PHORA-USE Registry (PHORAR) is a prospective, multicenter observational registry designed to collect real-world clinical data from adult and pediatric patients with PAH receiving routine clinical care. The purpose of this registry is to create a centralized database that can be used to better understand patient characteristics, treatment patterns, disease progression, and clinical outcomes. Information collected through the registry will support observational analyses aimed at identifying factors associated with outcomes and may contribute to the development of improved risk assessment and treatment strategies for patients with PAH.
primary_outcomes: Overall survival among participants with pulmonary arterial hypertension
title: PHORA-USE Registry (PHORAR)

brief_summary:
Schizophrenia-spectrum disorders (SSDs; schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, etc.) are among the most disabling and costly conditions globally. Most SSD medications treat symptoms like hallucinations and delusions, but cognitive symptoms, or problems with thinking, memory, and problem solving, remain untreated by medication. Other developing treatments for these symptoms include noninvasive stimulation of cognitive brain regions and behavioral therapies involving mental skill-building activities. While both of these treatments appear to improve cognitive symptoms, effects are inconsistent depending on specific details of the trial. Growing evidence suggests that using these therapies together could lead to larger, clinically meaningful effects. Still, prior combined therapy trials use simplified versions of the behavioral therapy, omitting the guidance of a therapist to engage and challenge the participant. These previous trials show some evidence for beneficial effects, particularly in working memory, but the omission of a therapist could limit effects. This study will be the first to test if using a comprehensive, therapist-guided behavioral therapy can amplify the effects of noninvasive brain stimulation (NIBS) to reduce cognitive symptoms and change brain activity in SSDs. We will conduct a small pilot study to gather preliminary evidence for this combined therapy using 10 participants split into 2 groups. One group will receive NIBS and comprehensive cognitive therapy (NIBS+) while the other receives NIBS and performs quizzes without the guidance of a therapist (NIBS-). Participants will receive therapies for 10 days over 2 weeks with 2 hours of therapy per day. We will compare interventions through the following aims. Aim 1 will examine changes in brain connections after NIBS+ and NIBS-. We will collect data from electrical brain recordings (electroencephalography/EEG) before and after interventions. We expect that connections between cognitive brain regions will be most strengthened by NIBS+ compared to NIBS-. Aim 2 will investigate what kind of cognitive symptoms are affected by NIBS+ and NIBS-. We will perform cognitive tests before and after the interventions. We expect that all cognitive symptoms (memory, motor speed, language skills, attention, processing speed, and planning abilities) will be most improved by NIBS+ compared to NIBS-, but that the largest improvements will be in short-term, active memory skills ("working memory"). We will also investigate if there is a relationship between the changes in brain connections and cognitive improvements.

This preliminary study will provide early evidence that the effects of noninvasive brain stimulation can be strengthened by a structured, therapist-guided behavioral therapy for cognitive symptoms. This will support the development of a new, combined therapy for untreated cognitive symptoms in schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. We will use findings of this study to support a trial proposal to the National Institute of Mental Health to test this therapy in a larger group of individuals.
primary_outcomes: Functional connectivity with the prefrontal cortex
title: Cognitive Augmentation, Remediation, and TDCS for Schizophrenia

brief_summary:
1. What is the purpose of this clinical trial?

   All of the participants in this trial have been diagnosed with a stroke or transitoric ischaemic attack within 72 hours of inclusion. Strokes are usually caused by a blood clot, which subsequently leads to a blockage of a blood vessel in the brain. In more than 20% of patients who have had a stroke or a transient ischemic attack (TIA, a temporary reduction in blood flow to the brain), atrial fibrillation (AF) is detectable on the electrocardiogram (ECG) as a possible cause. AF is a cardiac arrhythmia characterized by irregular activity in the atria, affecting a total of 1-2% of the population. This means that approximately 100,000 people in Austria are affected. AF is also an age-related cardiac arrhythmia, so that its prevalence is already 6% among people over 65 and up to 20% among those over 80. The risk of a recurrent stroke is five times higher in patients with AF; however, this risk can be significantly reduced through the use of blood-thinning medications. However, many patients suffer from "silent" atrial fibrillation-which they themselves do not notice-that may go undetected using standard monitoring methods in the hospital or, later, on an outpatient basis. Standard monitoring methods consist of a resting electrocardiogram (ECG) upon admission to the hospital, the ECG recorded during the first few days of hospitalization in the stroke unit, and usually also a long-term ECG (Holter ECG monitoring, typically over 24 hours) performed as part of further inpatient treatment; the latter can be repeated on an outpatient basis after discharge. These measures can improve the detection rate of AF. One problem, however, is that time gaps arise between the individual monitoring steps, which means that a AF episode may go unnoticed. Since 2016, international treatment guidelines have also recommended extended, continuous ECG monitoring. One option available for this purpose is the implantable loop recorder (ILR), which is implanted under the skin and continuously records an ECG (loop = without interruption) for 3-5 years. The goal of this study is to investigate whether the early implantation of a loop recorder-already in the stroke unit-can detect atrial fibrillation to a greater extent than conventional, routine standard monitoring, and thereby prevent the occurrence of a recurrent stroke within one year. For this, it is necessary that 1) two groups be formed through random assignment and 2) a control magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan of the skull be performed after 12 months to detect even "silent" strokes.
2. How does the clinical trial work, what is an implantable loop recorder, and how is it implanted?

The trial is being conducted at several hospitals in Austria. The departments leading the trial at the AKH are the Departments of Cardiology and Neurology. The aim of the study is to determine whether continuous ECG monitoring, initiated early-shortly after the stroke-can detect sudden-onset atrial fibrillation more frequently or earlier than a routine monitoring regimen used in everyday clinical practice. Half of all patients enrolled in the study will have a loop recorder implanted while they are still in the stroke unit, within the first 5 days after the stroke. The loop recorder is an established standard of care. This decision is made randomly (2 groups). The loop recorder is usually implanted on the left side of the chest during a minor surgical procedure. At this site, the doctor makes a small incision (approximately 1 cm long) under local anesthesia, through which the loop recorder is inserted directly under the skin. The incision is closed with sterile adhesive strips (rarely with a suture). A commercially available loop recorder from Abbott®, which has been used for this indication for several years, will be used-specifically, the "Assert-IQ" model. The loop recorder transmits events recorded daily to a network via the cellular network. Within this network, the physician can access patient data and take action as needed. The procedure typically takes only a few minutes and is minimally invasive. The loop recorder is used only for recording and documenting, not for treating cardiac arrhythmias. Once the wound has healed, malfunctions of the device are rare. However, external factors (e.g., electrical devices) can cause the loop recorder to malfunction.

More frequent detection of atrial fibrillation is expected as a result of more intensive ECG monitoring using an implantable loop recorder (ILR). In patients with AF following a stroke, oral anticoagulation with Marcumar or a related medication is associated with a significant reduction in the risk of recurrent strokes. We anticipate that, as a result, a larger proportion of patients will be treated with oral anticoagulants, which will in turn reduce the risk of recurrent strokes.
primary_outcomes: Stroke recurrence
title: Gapless ECG-Monitoring for Stroke Prevention by Atrial Fibrillation Detection (GEMS-PAF-randomized Trial) - A Multi-centre, Randomized Controlled Outcome Trial.

brief_summary:
The purpose of this clinical trial is to compare two surgical approaches used during primary hip replacement surgery (hip arthroplasty): the modified direct lateral approach and the modified anterolateral approach. Both surgical approaches are performed while the patient is lying on their side (the lateral decubitus position).

Hip replacement surgery is an established treatment for severe hip joint conditions such as end-stage hip osteoarthritis, helping to reduce pain and improve physical function and quality of life. Different surgical pathways to reach the hip joint interact differently with the surrounding hip abductor muscles, which may affect early recovery, walking ability, and daily physical function.

In this study, 300 adult participants (aged 18 years and older) scheduled for primary total hip replacement or partial hip replacement (hemiarthroplasty) at Assiut University Hospital will be randomly assigned, like flipping a coin, to one of two equal groups:

* Modified Direct Lateral Approach Group: Participants will undergo hip replacement using the modified Hardinge approach, which reaches the hip joint from the side and involves partially splitting and elevating the front portion of the hip abductor muscle tendon.
* Modified Anterolateral Approach Group: Participants will undergo hip replacement using the modified Watson-Jones approach, which reaches the hip joint through a natural space between two muscles at the front-side of the hip without splitting the abductor muscle.

Before surgery and at follow-up visits 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months after surgery, participants will complete the Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (HOOS) questionnaire to evaluate their ability to perform activities of daily living. Researchers will also examine hip X-rays to check implant positioning and monitor participants for any surgical complications for up to 1 year after surgery.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (HOOS) Activities of Daily Living (ADL) Subscale Score
title: Clinical Outcomes of the Modified Direct Lateral Approach Versus the Modified Anterolateral Approach in Hip Arthroplasty Performed in the Lateral Decubitus Position

brief_summary:
The TAILOR study aims to determine whether personalized antiplatelet therapy can reduce the risk of recurrent major cardiovascular events in patients who have experienced (a non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke).

Antiplatelet medications, such as aspirin and clopidogrel, are commonly prescribed to prevent stroke recurrence. However, some patients do not respond adequately to these medications and may remain at increased risk of further cardiovascular events.

The study will compare two approaches to antiplatelet therapy: standard care, in which medications are prescribed according to current clinical practice, and personalized care (tailored care), in which treatment is adjusted based on a blood test measuring how effectively the medication inhibits platelet activity.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of these two treatment strategies and followed for 12 months.

The main hypothesis is that tailoring antiplatelet therapy according to individual platelet response will be more effective than standard care in preventing recurrent ischemic stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular death. The study will also explore potential differences in treatment response between women and men.
primary_outcomes: Major Cardiovascular Event at 12 months
title: Personalized Antiplatelet Therapy to Prevent Recurrent Cardiovascular Events in After Ischemic Stroke

brief_summary: This randomized double-blind controlled trial aims to compare the effects of two different doses of intraoperative intravenous dexamethasone (4 mg versus 8 mg) versus placebo on perioperative glycemic response in adult patients with diabetes mellitus undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
primary_outcomes: Maximum Perioperative Blood Glucose Concentration
title: Dexamethasone Doses and Glycemic Response in Diabetic Cholecystectomy

brief_summary: Phase II, open-label, multicentre, multi-cohort platform study to determine the efficacy and safety of Datopotamab Deruxtecan (Dato-DXd)-based combinations for the treatment of TROP2 NMR+ NSCLC.
primary_outcomes: PFS as assessed by investigator on Treatment A
PFS as assessed by investigator on Treatment B
title: A Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of Dato-DXd-based Combinations in Participants With TROP2 NMR+ NSCLC

brief_summary: This is a prospective, multicenter, open-label, single-arm phase II clinical study evaluating the efficacy and safety of ivonescimab (a PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody) combined with Iza-bren (BL-B01D1; izalontamab brengitecan, an EGFR×HER3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate) in patients aged ≥18 years with histologically or cytologically confirmed unresectable locally advanced (stage IIIB/IIIC) or metastatic (stage IV) non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring EGFR-sensitizing mutations (exon 19 deletion or L858R) who have imaging-confirmed disease progression during or after prior third-generation EGFR-TKI therapy. A total of 43 subjects will be enrolled at 3 centers. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival (PFS). Other efficacy endpoints include ORR, confirmed ORR, DCR, DoR, OS, 6- and 12-month PFS rates, and 12- and 24-month OS rates. Safety and tolerability will be assessed, and exploratory analyses will evaluate immune markers, HER3 expression, and EGFR resistance molecular subtypes in relation to clinical efficacy. Treatment is given every 3 weeks: ivonescimab 20 mg/kg intravenously on Day 1; Iza-bren 2.5 mg/kg intravenously on Days 1 and 8. Ivonescimab is infused first, followed by Iza-bren after an interval of ≥30 minutes. Treatment continues until disease progression, intolerable toxicity, initiation of new anti-cancer therapy, death, withdrawal of consent, or a maximum of 24 months of treatment.
lead_sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University, School of Medicine
primary_outcomes: Progression-Free Survival (PFS)
title: A Phase II Study of Ivonescimab Combined With Iza-bren in Patients With Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.

brief_summary:
This study will identify and evaluate innovative approaches to leverage malaria vaccine visits as opportunities to enhance the delivery of other child health services in Rarieda sub-county, Siaya County, Kenya where RTS,S became part of their routine childhood immunization programs in 2019. Using a human-centred design approach, the implementation research will be conducted in two phases.

Phase 1 (Diagnose and Design) will consist of formative research to understand current practices, barriers, and facilitators for childhood health and malaria interventions using the WHO's behavioural and social drivers' framework for immunization. Having identified the barriers and facilitators to uptake, the investigators will prioritize drivers and develop innovations for implementation in collaboration with communities, healthcare workers and managers.

Phase 2 (Implement and Evaluate) will focus on implementing and evaluating the innovations developed in Phase 1. Using the RE-AIM (Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance) Framework, the study will assess the extent to which the interventions reach the target population, effectiveness of leveraging the malaria vaccine to increase uptake of other child health interventions, the extent of adoption by key stakeholders, and the fidelity and quality of implementation. The investigators will also explore cost and long-term sustainability.

The study will employ a mixed-methods approach, leveraging quantitative and qualitative data from health facility records, surveys, interviews, and observations.

The investigators will generate evidence on leveraging malaria vaccine visits and activities through: (i) innovative implementation strategies designed to maximize immunizations, child health interventions, and malaria prevention uptake; (ii) community engagement as an approach to optimize vaccine uptake and coverage; (iii) detailed qualitative data on the acceptability, perceptions, and barriers to uptake of vaccines and child health interventions; (iv) approaches to ensure access for zero-dose, under-vaccinated and underserved populations.
interventions: Community Health Promoters identify and refer under-vaccinated children to health facilities
Enhanced defaulter tracing with use of mobile technology
Strengthening immunization systems, health services, and interdepartmental collaboration
primary_outcomes: Reach
Effectiveness
Adoption
Implementation
Maintenance
title: Strategies to Improve RTS,S-4 Uptake and Integration With Other Child Health Services

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to find out whether the quantitative results of DOlab software (DaT-SPECT workflow) agree with the visual reading of brain scans performed by nuclear medicine physicians. The scans are 123I-ioflupane DaT-SPECT images of adults who were evaluated for dopamine transporter dysfunction, a condition seen in Parkinson's disease, other parkinsonian syndromes and dementia with Lewy bodies.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do the visual scores given by expert readers (0 = normal to 3 = marked abnormality) correlate with the values calculated by the software?
* Does using the software report change or refine the readers' classification compared with visual reading alone?
* How usable do readers find the software?

The study uses existing scans of 120 patients collected between January 2015 and May 2025 at two Italian hospitals. No new tests or treatments are given to participants, and the software results are not used for their clinical care.
primary_outcomes: Correlation between visual score and DOlab quantitative metrics
title: Correlation Between Visual Reading and DOlab Software Quantitative Analysis of DaT-SPECT Images

brief_summary:
The purpose of this clinical study is to evaluate the effects of a digital cognitive training program combined with physical activity on the cognitive and physical functions of community-dwelling older adults. For older adults, maintaining both mental and physical health is essential for overall well-being. This study hypothesizes that combining tablet-based brain exercises with short, physical activities will help improve participants' memory, thinking skills, and physical abilities, such as balance and walking.

Researchers aim to enroll approximately 35 community-dwelling older adults who are 65 years of age or older and capable of walking. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups:

1. Standard Intervention Group: Participants will attend a 50-minute session once a week for 10 weeks. During each session, they will use a tablet device for cognitive training focused on memory, attention, and executive functions. This training will be paused three times per session for about 3 minutes each to perform low-intensity, physical activities to music.
2. Extended Intervention Group: Participants will participate in the same 10-week digital cognitive training and physical activity program as the standard group. In addition, they will receive additional home-based cognitive activities to complete once a week.

To measure the effectiveness of the program, researchers will assess all participants before the program starts and after the 10-week program ends. Assessments will evaluate cognitive function, including memory and attention, as well as physical functions, such as grip strength, leg strength, balance, walking speed, and muscle mass.
interventions: Standard Digital Cognitive and Physical Training
Extended Digital Cognitive and Physical Training
primary_outcomes: The Korean Version of Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA-K)
title: Digital Cognitive Training in Older Adults

brief_summary:
Pleural infections are common and associated with significant illness and healthcare burden, often requiring hospitalization, antibiotics, chest tube drainage, and sometimes surgery. Intrapleural enzyme therapy (IET), which involves administering two medications, alteplase (10 mg) and DNase (5md), directly into the pleural space through a chest tube, has been shown to improve drainage of infected fluid, reduce the need for surgical referral, and shorten hospital stays based in a clinical trial. Alteplase dosing has ever been determined through formal dose-finding studies. It remains unclear whether lower doses may provide similar benefits.

The DREAMS trial aims to determine whether a lower dose of alteplase can achieve comparable treatment outcomes, while potentially reducing medication-related risks.

Participants will:

* Be admitted to the hospital for management of a pleural infection and receive routine medical care, including chest tube drainage of infected fluid and medications through the chest tube
* Be asked to provide a consent to participate in the study
* Be randomly assigned (akin to a coin flip) to receive 4m mg versus 10 mg alteplase, both in combination with DNase.
primary_outcomes: Treatment Success
title: Dose Reduced Alteplase in Managing Intrapleural Sepsis

brief_summary:
This study aimed to evaluate changes in medication adherence, blood pressure, and health-related quality of life following a pharmacist-led intervention among hypertensive patients with comorbidities in Bhutan.

A single-group, pre-post quasi-experimental study was conducted at Phuentsholing General Hospital, Bhutan. Participants received pharmacist-led counseling and education focusing on hypertension management, medication adherence, prevention of complications, and lifestyle modifications. Assessments were conducted at three time points: baseline, first follow-up (approximately two months), and second follow-up (approximately four months).

Medication adherence was assessed using the Adherence to Refills and Medications Scale (ARMS), while blood pressure was measured using an automated blood pressure monitoring device. Health-related quality of life was evaluated using the EQ-5D-5L questionnaire and EQ Visual Analogue Scale (EQ-VAS). Changes in these outcomes were assessed across the three assessment periods.

The study was designed to provide evidence on changes in medication adherence, clinical outcomes, and health-related quality of life associated with pharmacist-led counseling and education among hypertensive patients with comorbidities in Bhutan.
interventions: Pharmacist-Led Counseling and education for Hypertension Management
primary_outcomes: Change in Medication Adherence
Change in Blood Pressure
title: "PhaRmacist-led Intervention for Medication adherencE and Clinical Outcomes Among HyperTenSive Patients With Comorbidities in BHUTAN (PRIME-HTN-BHUTAN).

brief_summary:
Hamstring inflexibility is common among young football players and may negatively affect athletic performance, particularly agility. Stretching exercises are commonly used to improve hamstring flexibility; however, the effectiveness of stretching performed with a pressure biofeedback unit on agility performance has not been sufficiently investigated.

The aim of this study is to examine the effect of hamstring stretching performed with a pressure biofeedback unit on agility performance in young male football players with hamstring inflexibility. Participants will be allocated to an experimental group performing hamstring stretching exercises with a pressure biofeedback unit and a control group receiving no intervention.

Agility performance and hamstring flexibility will be assessed before and after the intervention period. The findings of this study are expected to contribute to the understanding of effective stretching strategies for improving performance in football players.
conditions: Hamstring Inflexibility Agility Performance in Young Male Football Players
primary_outcomes: Agility Performance
title: Effect of Pressure Biofeedback-Assisted Hamstring Stretching on Agility in Young Male Football Players

brief_summary:
Percutaneous Epidural Neuroplasty (PEN) is a minimally invasive treatment option used for the management of back and neck pain.

The investigators aimed to evaluate the effects of different saline concentrations (0.9%, 5%, 10%) used during the cervical PEN procedure on post-procedure NRS and NDI scores.
primary_outcomes: Comparison of the effect of percutaneous cervical epidural neurolysis in the acute phase with baseline NRS scores
Comparison of the effects of different salin concentrations used in cervical epidural neurolysis on NDI and NRS scores
title: Which One Should Be Preferred In Epidural Neuroplasty?

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial will investigate the acute (immediate) effects of a single session of manual myofascial release applied to lower extremity muscles on squat jump height and lower extremity joint kinematics in healthy young adults aged 18-40 years. Sixty volunteers will be randomly assigned to a myofascial release group or a control (rest) group. After a standardized warm-up, all participants will perform three maximal squat jumps. The intervention group will then receive standardized bilateral manual myofascial release to predetermined lower extremity muscle groups, while the control group will rest for an equivalent period. Squat jump testing will then be repeated under identical conditions. Jump height will be measured with the validated smartphone application My Jump 2, and hip, knee and ankle kinematics during the jump will be recorded with a Microsoft Kinect-based markerless motion analysis system.
primary_outcomes: Change in squat jump height
title: Acute Effects of Myofascial Release on Squat Jump Performance

brief_summary:
The Stiff Ankle Project is a prospective, cross-sectional study conducted at UCLouvain within the Institute of Experimental and Clinical Research (IREC/NMSK). The study aims to improve understanding of how the passive mechanical properties and active neuromuscular function of the foot-ankle complex influence running biomechanics, performance, and potential injury risk in healthy runners.

The project is based on the concept that the foot and ankle act both as a spring, capable of storing and releasing energy, and as a lever that contributes to propulsion during running. The primary objective is to integrate measures of tendon stiffness, neuromuscular function, foot morphology, and running biomechanics into a comprehensive framework explaining the role of the foot-ankle complex in running performance and injury mechanisms. A secondary objective is to establish a normative database in healthy runners.

Healthy adult runners aged 18 to 35 years with at least one year of regular running experience and a minimum weekly running volume of 15 km will be recruited. Participants must be free from lower-limb injuries for at least six months. Individuals with a history of Achilles tendon rupture, major foot or ankle surgery, or neurological or musculoskeletal conditions affecting running will be excluded.

Participants will attend three laboratory sessions. Assessments will include measurements of foot morphology, passive stiffness, aerobic fitness, running economy, running biomechanics, muscle activity, and neuromuscular performance. Running tests will be performed both barefoot and shod at individualized speeds. Additional evaluations will include strength, endurance, power, hopping, and jumping tests to establish a comprehensive functional profile of the foot-ankle complex.

The findings are expected to improve understanding of the role of the foot-ankle complex in running and to support the development of individualized approaches for performance enhancement, injury prevention, and rehabilitation.
primary_outcomes: Foot-Ankle Neuromuscular strength
Foot-Ankle Neuromuscular endurance
Pantar flexors power
Foot-ankle reactive strength
Ankle braking power
Ankle Propulsive power
Late stance foot stiffness
title: Passive Mechanical Stiffness Properties and Active Neuromuscular Function of the Foot and Ankle Complex Influence on Running Biomechanics

brief_summary:
After myocardial infarction (MI), reduced LVEF (≤35%) is a known risk marker for sudden cardiac death (SCD), yet many SCD cases occur with LVEF \>35% as myocardial scarring remains a strong arrhythmogenic substrate regardless of preserved function. Non-sustained ventricular tachycardias ((NS)VTs) predict malignant arrhythmias and highlight the importance of early detection.

The primary objective is to determine whether continuous cardiac rhythm monitoring after myocardial infarction improves the detection of cardiac arrhythmias that require medical intervention by conducting a prospective, multi-center, international, randomized trial.
lead_sponsor: Academisch Medisch Centrum - Universiteit van Amsterdam (AMC-UvA)
primary_outcomes: Time to first documented cardiac arrhythmia prompting medical intervention
title: Comparison of Continuous Cardiac Rhythm Monitoring and Standard Care in Post-MI Patients With Significant Scar and Reduced LVEF

brief_summary:
Long bone fractures can cause significant anxiety in adult patients attending the Emergency Department. Anxiety may occur while patients wait for further treatment, admission, or surgery.

This study evaluated the effectiveness of Jacobson's Progressive Muscle Relaxation Technique (JPMR) in reducing fracture-related anxiety among adult patients with long bone fractures in the Emergency Department of Rashid Hospital Trauma Center, Dubai, United Arab Emirates.

The study used a non-randomized controlled design. Eligible adult patients were allocated to an intervention group or a control group. Participants in the intervention group received Jacobson's Progressive Muscle Relaxation Technique in addition to routine care, while participants in the control group received routine care.

Fracture-related anxiety was assessed using the Fracture-Specific Anxiety Scale (FSAS). Pain was also assessed using a Visual Analogue Scale (VAS).

The study compared anxiety levels before and after the intervention and between the intervention and control groups. The findings were intended to help determine whether JPMR may be a useful supportive intervention for managing fracture-related anxiety in the Emergency Department.
primary_outcomes: Change in Fracture-Related Anxiety Scores Measured Using the Fracture-Specific Anxiety Scale (FSAS)
title: Effectiveness of Jacobson's Progressive Muscle Relaxation Technique (JPMR) on Fracture-Related Anxiety in Adult Patients With Long Bone Fractures in the Emergency Department

brief_summary:
The rising burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) among people living with HIV (PLWH) poses significant challenges to healthcare systems. Addressing this dual disease burden requires a transition from vertical, disease-specific programs to comprehensive patient-centered integrated chronic care models. However, resource constraints, fragmented service delivery, and limited patient engagement impede progress. Mobile health (mHealth) interventions have emerged as a promising strategy to enhance self-management, foster peer support, and improve patient engagement in the context of HIV-NCD multimorbidity.

The pre-post interventional trial aims to evaluate the HIVE interventions framework in the management of long-term conditions such as non-communicable diseases and mental health conditions, among PLWH. The HIVE interventions comprise a mobile health application (HIVE App), tools that enhance integrated NCD care management and interpersonal support. Up to 260 PLWH will be enrolled from clinical sites from four countries: Greece, Kazakhstan, Kenya and Malta. Following the baseline visit, they will be followed for one year with 3 follow-up visits every four months. The primary outcome of interest is a significant improvement in self-management capability among PLWH with at least one NCD, as measured by the Appraisal of Self-Care Agency Scale-Revised (ASAS-R) scores. Secondary outcomes include the significant improvement in self-efficacy for managing medications and symptoms of chronic conditions (PROMIS), Health-related Quality of Life (HRQOL), awareness of NCD and mental health assessment scores (GAD-7 and PHQ-9).

This HIVE trial also incorporates evaluation of the implementation processes and implementation outcomes of the HIVE interventions. The Nonadoption, Abandonment, Scale-up, Spread and Sustainability (NASSS) framework will guide the assessment of barriers and facilitators of the HIVE interventions, with particular focus on adoption, engagement and acceptability, cost-effectiveness analysis and social impact analysis. NASSS domains will be evaluated through a survey and at least two focus group discussions with participants from all four sites. Additionally, semi-structured interviews will be held with healthcare professionals at the sites to explore their perspectives on the patients' adoption and acceptability to the HIVE interventions, as well as their perspectives on the integration of the implementation framework in NCD care.
conditions: Implementation of Integrated Care for People Living With HIV and Multiple Long-Term Conditions
interventions: Integration of NCD Care Into HIV Clinics
primary_outcomes: Change in Self-Management Capability Assessed Using the Appraisal of Self-Care Agency Scale-Revised (ASAS-R)
title: The HIVE Trial: Improving Care for People Living With HIV and Chronic Conditions

brief_summary:
This study will be conducted at HMHI's treatment resisted mood disorder clinic (TRMD) and will collect data from patient's receiving ketamine infusion treatments (KIT) for TRD. Data will be collected for two separate cohorts, representing two different stages in treatment, acute series (initial 6-12 session) and maintenance (will collect data from up to 6 maintenance sessions).

The goal of the study will be to explore to role of music in this treatment modality and how personal choice and properties of music played during the treatments affects experiential and clinical outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptoms
title: Analysis of Music in Ketamine Infusion Therapy

brief_summary:
Formaldehyde exposure is common in some occupational environments, including anatomy laboratories, and may affect respiratory health. However, the early biological changes caused by short-term high-concentration formaldehyde exposure remain unclear.

This prospective self-controlled observational study aims to evaluate the effects of short-term high-concentration formaldehyde exposure on respiratory microecology, inflammatory biomarkers, and acute respiratory symptoms in healthy adults. Participants will be monitored before and after formaldehyde exposure, and changes in airway-related biological indicators will be assessed through biological samples and clinical evaluations.

The findings of this study may provide human evidence for exposure control, ventilation improvement, protective measures, and health risk assessment in environments with formaldehyde exposure.
lead_sponsor: First Affiliated Hospital of Ningbo University
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in the Shannon Diversity Index of Induced Sputum Microbiota
title: Effects of Short-Term High-Concentration Formaldehyde Exposure on Respiratory Microecology and Inflammatory Markers in Healthy Adults

brief_summary: Insomnia and depression are highly prevalent during postpartum, but effective treatment options are severely limited. Perinatal Understanding of Mindful Awareness (PUMAS) combines behavioral sleep strategies and mindfulness-based exercises to improve sleep and mood during pregnancy. Indeed, PUMAS has been shown to effectively treatment comorbid insomnia and depression in pregnancy in controlled and uncontrolled trials. The present randomized controlled trial (RCT) will evaluate the effectiveness of PUMAS in a sample of postpartum women with comorbid insomnia and depression who will be randomized to to telemedicine PUMAS or online sleep hygiene education (SHE; enhanced usual care). Patients will be treated for six weeks followed by assessment after treatment then follow-up assessment 3-months later. The investigators hypothesize that PUMAS patients, relative to SHE patients, will report superior acute treatment effects on insomnia and depression as well as more durable effects at 3-month follow-up.
interventions: Perinatal Understanding of Mindful Awareness for Sleep (PUMAS)
primary_outcomes: Insomnia Severity Index (ISI)
title: Healing and Improving Postnatal Nights Through Sleep (HIPNoS)

brief_summary:
SATISCHOL is a prospective, monocentric observational study designed to assess pain management and quality of care in patients undergoing elective cholecystectomy at Limoges University Hospital, France.

The primary objective is to assess the proportion of patients reporting a visual analogue scale (VAS) pain score below 4 two hours after surgery, in association with the occurrence of no postoperative complication or a grade I early postoperative complication according to the Clavien-Dindo classification, within four weeks after surgery.

Secondary objectives include assessing early postoperative pain, describing postoperative complications and intraoperative pain management techniques, and evaluating changes in patients' quality of life using the Gastrointestinal Quality of Life Index (GIQLI) and EQ-5D-5L questionnaires. Patient-reported experience will also be assessed using a study-specific questionnaire (PREMS).

brief_summary: Awake deep brain stimulation (DBS) is an effective surgical treatment for Parkinson's disease and other movement disorders, but patients remain at high risk of falls after surgery because of gait disturbance, postural instability, cognitive decline and transient postoperative delirium. This project/research is supported within the scope of the "2209-A University Students Research Projects Support Program" 2025/1 term conducted by the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Türkiye (TÜBİTAK) Scientist Support Programs Directorate (BİDEB).

The post-exercise recovery process in athletes is a critical process in terms of the sustainability of performance, the effectiveness of physiological adaptation, and the prevention of overload-related injuries. Microtraumatic damage occurring in muscle tissue during exercise, depletion of energy stores, and neuromechanical fatigue lead to disruption of homeostatic balance. Therefore, the effectiveness of recovery is a determining factor both in maintaining performance and sustaining musculoskeletal health. In the literature, it has been demonstrated that in the absence of appropriate recovery strategies, the risk of injury increases due to reductions in the viscoelastic properties of the muscle-tendon complex and deterioration in proprioceptive control.

In recent years, vibrating foam roller applications have attracted attention among innovative approaches supporting recovery. While the conventional foam roller supports recovery by reducing muscle tone and increasing blood flow, the vibrating version has been suggested to accelerate neuromuscular relaxation by enhancing proprioceptive feedback. However, the current evidence regarding the effects of this method is limited, and most studies have focused only on acute outcomes. This project aims to comparatively investigate the short- and mid-term effects of vibrating and non-vibrating foam roller applications on recovery in young-adult athletes with exercise-induced muscle damage.

Athletes included in the project will be randomly assigned into two groups after delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) is induced in the gastrocnemius muscle through a standardized eccentric plantar flexion protocol. Group 1 will receive a vibrating foam roller application, whereas Group 2 will receive a non-vibrating foam roller application. The level of delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) will be assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) immediately after the application, at 24 hours, 48 hours, and at the end of the first week. In addition, the passive mechanical properties of the muscle related to the recovery process will be evaluated non-invasively from the gastrocnemius muscle using the MyotonPRO device. Data will be analyzed using a Two-Way Repeated Measures ANOVA to examine the interaction between time and group factors. Sample size was determined as 40 participants with 80% power using G\*Power software.

The project will be conducted by a team experienced in the field of sports physiotherapy, and the processes of data collection, analysis, and reporting will be planned in accordance with the research timeline. It is anticipated that the findings obtained will contribute to the development of an evidence-based and low-cost recovery method in the field of sports physiotherapy.

The study will investigate differences in ultrasound characteristics among lymphoma subtypes, evaluate changes in ultrasound features during treatment, and develop and validate prediction models integrating imaging and clinical information. The main hypothesis is that multimodal ultrasound features and their early treatment-related changes reflect the biological heterogeneity of lymphoma and can improve noninvasive lymphoma classification and early prediction of treatment response.

The study will also assess other acne lesions, overall acne severity, skin oiliness, hydration, elasticity, skin surface characteristics, and skin thickness using clinical examinations and specialized instruments. Skin tolerability and any adverse events will also be monitored.

Participants will undergo assessments before treatment, after three completed treatments, two weeks after the fifth treatment, and approximately two months later.

brief_summary:
The Ross procedure entails pulmonary autograft replacement of the aortic valve, primarily indicated in pediatric and young adult cohorts presenting with severe aortic valve disease. Despite postoperative preservation of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) on resting transthoracic echocardiography, a subset of recipients exhibits blunted peak oxygen consumption (peak VO2), subclinical electromechanical dyssynchrony, and ventricular arrhythmias.

Chronic severe aortic valve pathology induces distinct myocardial remodeling patterns. Chronic pressure overload (aortic stenosis) triggers concentric cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and diffuse interstitial fibrosis. Chronic volume overload (aortic regurgitation) induces eccentric left ventricular dilatation and extracellular matrix degradation with collagen disarray. Following surgical hemodynamic unloading, left ventricular mass regresses; however, the extent of diffuse interstitial collagen matrix resorption versus pure cardiomyocyte cellular volume regression remains uncharacterized in this demographic.

This prospective longitudinal study employs multiparametric cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging to evaluate myocardial tissue characterization and deformation kinetics in young adults undergoing the Ross procedure. Participants will undergo contrast-enhanced CMR at baseline and at 12 months postoperatively. Quantitative endpoints include native T1 mapping, extracellular volume fraction (ECV), indexed extracellular volume (iECV), and three-dimensional (3D) feature-tracking strain (global longitudinal, circumferential, and radial strain). The primary objective is to correlate the resolution of diffuse microscopic fibrosis with subclinical mechanical recovery, comparing remodeling trajectories between pressure-overloaded and volume-overloaded phenotypes.
primary_outcomes: Diffuse myocardial fibrosis
Diffuse myocardial fibrosis
title: Myocardial Fibrosis and Deformation Kinetics After the Ross Procedure Using Cardiac MRI

brief_summary: A retinal detachment is a vision-threatening condition that most often requires surgical treatment. In this study, the investigators will test a new treatment for retinal detachment. The investigators will use a special needle to inject a gel between the layers of the eye wall to block off the breaks in the retina and heal the detachment. The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether cold-water immersion of the ankle changes muscle tone, joint mobility, strength, balance, skin temperature and thermal comfort in physically active adults aged 18 to 40 years with and without a history of ankle sprain, and whether these responses differ between the two groups.

Participants will be assessed at rest (control condition), then immerse the foot and ankle in cold water (10 to 15 °C) up to mid-shin for 20 minutes, and be reassessed immediately after the immersion and again after 20 minutes of rest. brief_summary:
Brief Summary:

Many older adults in rural areas suffer from both type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure. Managing these two conditions at the primary care level is often challenging. This study aims to find out if a new "village doctor-led digital management model" can help improve patient health compared to the current standard care.

Who can participate? Adults aged 60 or older who have been diagnosed with both type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure, whose current blood sugar or blood pressure is not well-controlled, and who receive care at local village clinics.

How does the study work?

Village clinics will be randomly assigned to one of two groups:

Usual Care Group: Patients receive standard national primary health services.

Integrated Care Group: In addition to standard care, village doctors will use an Artificial Intelligence (AI) system. This system provides clinical suggestions to the village doctors, helps arrange remote consultations with hospital specialists if needed, and gives patients personalized advice on diet and exercise.

What are we measuring? We will follow participants for up to 3 years. The main goals are to see if the new AI-assisted model improves the control of blood sugar, blood pressure, and cholesterol at 12 months, and whether it reduces the risk of severe cardiovascular events (like heart attacks or strokes) over 36 months.

brief_summary:
This project is a two-phase, observational, cross-sectional study aiming to evaluate the relationships among food literacy, nutritional status, and gut microbiota profile in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

In the first phase of the project, the questionnaire developed by Ludwig et al. (2024) for individuals with T2DM will be adapted into Turkish, and its validity and reliability will be evaluated. In the second phase, the study aims to determine the relationship between the level of food literacy and structural characteristics of the gut microbiota, such as microbial diversity and the Bacillota/Bacteroidota ratio. In addition, potential associations between biomarkers reflecting intestinal barrier integrity and food literacy will be investigated. Furthermore, the relationship between participants' nutritional status and gut microbiota profile will be assessed, differences in microbiota composition across different body mass index (BMI) categories will be examined, and the association between food literacy level and indicators of glycemic control will be determined.

The study will be conducted among volunteer individuals attending the Obesity and Diabetes Outpatient Clinic of the Department of Endocrinology and Metabolism, İstanbul University-Cerrahpaşa Faculty of Medicine. Sociodemographic information, 24-hour dietary records, anthropometric measurements, body composition, physical activity level, routine biochemical parameters, intestinal permeability biomarkers (LPS, zonulin, occludin, and claudin), and stool samples will be collected from the participants. Data collection will be conducted at a single time point, and the findings obtained will be analyzed using appropriate statistical methods.

The originality of the project lies in its holistic approach to food literacy in T2DM management by considering it together with gut microbiota and indicators of metabolic control. In addition, the Turkish adaptation of the food literacy scale developed specifically for individuals with T2DM will contribute to the literature by providing a valid and reliable measurement instrument that can be used in this field.

The findings of the study are expected to contribute to the development of evidence-based intervention programs targeting the behavioral and biological management of T2DM by elucidating the relationships among food literacy level, glycemic control, dietary patterns, and microbial diversity.

Gut microbiota profile

brief_summary: TP53-mutated myeloid neoplasms encompass biologically heterogeneous disorders with frequent cytogenetic abnormalities and poor outcomes. In myelodysplastic neoplasms, TP53 allelic state contributes to clinical phenotype and prognosis. In acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndromes with excess blasts, molecular similarities support studying TP53-associated disease across conventional diagnostic boundaries, although pooling lower-risk and advanced diseases can introduce important clinical heterogeneity. Available therapies improve remission in some patients without reliably producing durable disease control. In a pooled analysis of poor-risk cytogenetic AML with TP53 mutations, azacitidine plus venetoclax increased remission compared with azacitidine alone without a corresponding improvement in survival. A recent molecular analysis of the pivotal CPX-351 trial found that benefit was concentrated in AML with myelodysplasia-related mutations rather than TP53-mutated AML. Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) can provide prolonged survival in selected patients, but its outcome depends on biological and clinical context. Retrospective transplant data support integrating VAF and cytogenetics, whereas biological-assignment data in MDS suggest that some patients with TP53 mutations benefit from transplantation. the investigators sought to describe treatment patterns and outcomes in a pooled TP53-associated clinical cohort and to explore cytogenetic abnormalities, TP53 mutation burden, co-mutation presence, and VAF. A secondary objective was to describe transplanted patients according to available pre-HCT TP53 VAF and to assess HCT as a time-dependent exposure. Our purpose was hypothesis generation rather than causal ranking of regimens or derivation of a validated transplant-selection rule.
primary_outcomes: Description of clinical outcomes according to treatment patterns
title: Treatment Outcomes and Molecular Prognostic Factors in TP53 Mutated Myeloid Neoplasms

brief_summary: This study investigates the effects of combined transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) on cognitive function and brain-visceral coupling in healthy adults, while exploring the underlying neural mechanisms. Participants will undergo four different neuromodulation conditions, including TMS stimulation, tACS stimulation, combined TMS-tACS stimulation, and sham stimulation. The order of stimulation sessions will be counterbalanced using a randomized Latin square design. During each experimental session, researchers will simultaneously record participants' electroencephalography (EEG), electrocardiography (ECG), respiratory, and gastric signals before and after stimulation, and evaluate cognitive performance through behavioral tasks following stimulation. The primary objective of this study is to investigate how different neuromodulation patterns influence brain-visceral coupling and cognitive function, and to further examine the relationship between changes in central-autonomic interactions and cognitive performance.
