brief_summary:
This study aims to compare the effects of conventional rehabilitation alone, conventional rehabilitation combined with task-oriented training, and conventional rehabilitation combined with virtual reality-assisted task-oriented training in individuals who have undergone primary unilateral total knee arthroplasty (TKA).

A total of 60 participants aged 50-75 years who begin rehabilitation between 7 and 14 days after surgery will be included in this prospective, three-arm, assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups:

Conventional Rehabilitation (CR)

Conventional Rehabilitation Plus Task-Oriented Training (CR+TOT)

Conventional Rehabilitation Plus Virtual Reality-Assisted Task-Oriented Training (CR+VR-TOT)

All participants will receive conventional rehabilitation for 45 minutes per session, three times per week for six weeks (18 sessions). The conventional rehabilitation program will include exercises to improve knee range of motion, muscle strength, walking ability, and functional mobility, as well as neuromuscular electrical stimulation. Cryotherapy will be applied at the end of each treatment session.

Participants in the task-oriented training group will receive an additional 15 minutes of functional exercises targeting activities such as standing up from a chair, weight shifting, stepping, walking, and changing direction. Participants in the virtual reality-assisted group will receive an additional 15 minutes of non-immersive virtual reality-based task-oriented training.

The primary outcome will be functional mobility, assessed using the Timed Up and Go Test. Secondary outcomes will include walking performance, sit-to-stand performance, knee-related pain and function, knee range of motion, lower extremity muscle strength, static balance, fear of movement, and pain catastrophizing.

All outcomes will be assessed before and after the six-week rehabilitation program. The study aims to determine whether adding task-oriented training or virtual reality-assisted task-oriented training to conventional rehabilitation improves short-term recovery following total knee arthroplasty.
interventions: Conventional Rehabilitation (CR) + Virtual Reality-Assisted Task-Oriented Training (VR-TOT)
primary_outcomes: Change in Functional Mobility Assessed by the Timed Up and Go Test (TUG)
title: Task-Oriented Training and Virtual Reality-Assisted Rehabilitation After Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Randomized Controlled Trial

A total of 44 eligible adult patients will be randomly allocated into two parallel groups (22 patients per group). The control group will receive standard FOLFOX chemotherapy, while the intervention group will receive standard FOLFOX chemotherapy plus oral lactoferrin (Pravotin) at a dose of 100 mg twice daily, starting from the first chemotherapy cycle and continuing throughout the planned chemotherapy course.

The study will evaluate peripheral neuropathy, gastrointestinal and hematological toxicities, oxidative stress and neuroprotective biomarkers.

brief_summary: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a high-risk prodromal stage of dementia, and impaired working memory is one of its core features. A single bout of exercise can transiently improve cognitive function, but whether different exercise modalities produce comparable effects remains unclear. This randomized, controlled, parallel-group trial will enroll 【N=125】 community-dwelling adults aged 60 years and older with MCI, who will be randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1:1 ratio to one of five groups: a 30-minute session of table tennis, elastic-band resistance training, brisk walking, Baduanjin, or a seated-rest control. Exercise intensity will be standardized at light-to-moderate intensity (【40-59】% of heart rate reserve; rating of perceived exertion 【10-13】). The primary outcome is working memory performance assessed immediately before and within 5 minutes after the session. Secondary outcomes include additional behavioral working memory indices and electroencephalographic (EEG) measures. Findings will inform the design of community-based, modality-specific exercise prescriptions for older adults with MCI.
primary_outcomes: N-back
Electroencephalographic (EEG) indices
title: Acute Effects of Table Tennis, Resistance Band Training, Brisk Walking, and Baduanjin on Working Memory in Older Adults With Mild Cognitive Impairment: an EEG-based Randomized Controlled Trial

Orbital floor fractures are common facial injuries that can lead to complications such as enophthalmos (sunken eye), diplopia (double vision), and restricted eye movement if left untreated. While autologous bone grafts are considered the gold standard, titanium mesh is widely used due to its biocompatibility and lack of a donor site. This randomized clinical study aims to determine which material provides better orbital structural support, bone healing, and functional outcomes with fewer complications.

brief_summary:
A key process in intensive care is the creation of transfer reports. These summarize the essential aspects of the treatment to date and ensure that information is passed on to the next treatment team in a structured manner. They contain, among other things, diagnoses, relevant examination results, and therapeutic measures that have been carried out. The aim of a transfer report is to document the patient's medical history and the course of treatment to date in a concise and complete manner. Incomplete transfer reports can lead to repeated examinations, which can potentially delay further therapy and endanger the patient, as well as incurring additional costs.

In this context, a complete transfer report ensures continuity of treatment and contributes significantly to patient safety.

Transfer reports are created from a synthesis of a large number of documents. In addition to medical facts from tables and free-text summaries, physicians also draw on their experience to pass on relevant information to future treatment teams in the synthesis of detailed documentation. This process naturally requires a great deal of time and concentration in patients receiving intensive care.

Artificial intelligence methods, such as large language models (LLMs), could be used to learn how to create transfer reports and formulate drafts.

LLMs can convert unstructured free text into a structured form, thereby facilitating the report creation process. This would make it possible to generate a pre-formulated draft that doctors could then review and supplement.

At present, transfer reports are created by physicians with considerable effort and time. The methods currently available for automating report generation are limited to text modules that largely bundle data sources deterministically. Some of these methods are already commercially available, but they are not capable of creating individual reports beyond form letters.

The automatic analysis of unstructured text data falls within a subfield of AI known as natural language processing (NLP), which also includes language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT and Gemini, which have been popular since 2022. A major milestone was reached with the development of the Transformer architecture in 2017, which, in addition to the availability of enormous amounts of training data (e.g., Wikipedia, news articles, or books), forms the basis for many groundbreaking language models. The effectiveness of these LLMs is limited for specific domains such as medicine, as the training data often lacks relevant characteristics such as complex terminology or writing styles. Adapting these models for clinical use to improve patient care, research, and medical education is a highly topical field of research. The most relevant foreign-language models include BioBERT, Meditron, and Med-PaLM. As of July 2024, there is only limited research on the development of German-language models, e.g., medBERT, BioGottBERT, and a few models that are not publicly available.

The sole use of LLMs is problematic due to non-reproducible results, lack of transparency, and bias in the models. Knowledge graphs (KGs) are used in medicine to represent and analyze complex information structures. The creation of a "robust digital patient twin" would be improved by the use of LLMs and KGs. This would allow the state of health to be assessed based on all digitally available clinical information (both structured and, in this project, now also unstructured). Recent studies confirm that adapted LLMs in the English language domain can produce summaries that are equivalent to or better than those produced by human experts, and that these are often difficult to distinguish from reports written by humans.

The legal framework for this results from a complex interaction of legal provisions from data protection law (with regard to health data), artificial intelligence law (AI Act), medical law (in particular hospital law), (medical) product law, medical professional law, and other relevant professional groups (e.g., nursing and pharmacy), as well as relevant civil and criminal law standards of care. In addition, there are fundamental rights requirements based on the ECHR and the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights. Data protection issues relating to the use of health data, in particular for research with AI systems, and professional law issues in connection with automated aggregation and presentation have already been examined in detail (as part of the SMARAGD project, FFG 872575).
primary_outcomes: Quality of Discharge Report Drafts
title: Generating Medical Discharge Report Drafts Via Artificial Intelligence

brief_summary:
Dementia is one of the major causes of disability and among older adults globally, with 6.7 million Americans living with Alzheimer's disease. Depression is common in people with cognitive and memory problems.

Depression in the elderly increases the risk of disability, medical comorbidity, cognitive impairment, and death. Patients with depression are at an increased risk of worsening cognition. Further, patients with depression are traditionally excluded from therapeutic trials in Alzheimer's Disease and other dementias. Current medications to treat depression in patients with dementia haven't been helpful. Effective approaches to treating depression in dementia are necessary.

Ketamine has been studied extensively for the treatment of depression. It produces a rapid antidepressant effect with improvement of depressive symptoms reported 2 hours after infusion that continues for several days. Due to its rapid action, ketamine has gathered significant public attention. Providers in the community are already administering this drug to patients with dementia based on anecdotal evidence without evidence of its safety or benefit. A fast, safe, and effective treatment of depression may reduce the rate of cognitive decline in patients with dementia and reduce depression burden and improve quality of life and function. As patients with depression are likely unable to receive disease modifying therapies for Alzheimer's Disease (lecanemab or donanemab) rapid improvement of depressive symptoms with ketamine could represent treatment that allows them to be able to receive these therapies faster.

This proposal, will examine the safety, tolerability and feasibility of administering IV ketamine for the treatment of depression in participants with Alzheimer's Disease as well as obtain preliminary data regarding the treatment benefit.

brief_summary:
Patients with pain in their low back that sometimes sends a shooting, sharp pain down their leg are usually diagnosed with lumbar radicular pain, or lumbar radiculopathy. MRIs are most commonly used to acquire images of the spine. The purpose of these images is to provide doctors with important information on what may be causing the low back pain and what treatment options may be the most effective in treating the pain. However, standard MRIs are taken when the patient is lying down, which may not be the most accurate representation of what the spine looks like in positions where patients experience pain, such as standing. A weight-bearing CT (WBCT) scan is a 3D imaging test that takes detailed pictures of the spine while patients are standing up. Unlike traditional MRI scans, where the patient lies down, this technology provides more information on how the spine looks when the patient is upright and participating in activities such as standing and walking. This information allows doctors to better understand the underlying causes of the pain and help guide targeted treatments to address those issues.

The Planmed XFI full-body weight-bearing CT scanner received 510(k) clearance from the FDA on September 26, 2025. This means the Planmed XFI® WBCT is safe and effective because it is substantially equivalent to a device already on the market.
primary_outcomes: Comparison of neutral WBCT position to prespecified clinical phenotype
title: Lumbar WBCT vs MRI

brief_summary:
Becoming a parent for the first time can bring uncertainty, stress, and concerns about caring for a newborn, particularly during the first weeks after birth. The ALMA-RN study will investigate whether an educational programme delivered through Instagram, alongside usual care, can reduce anxiety, parenting stress, and symptoms of depression in first-time mothers and fathers.

The study will take place at Hospital Universitario 12 de Octubre in Madrid, Spain. It will include 144 first-time parents aged 18 years or older whose babies are healthy, born at term, and do not require admission to a neonatal unit. One parent per family will participate.

Participants will be assigned by chance, with an equal likelihood, to one of two groups. One group will receive the usual information and support provided by healthcare professionals. The other group will receive the same usual care plus access to a private Instagram account offering a structured educational programme lasting approximately two weeks.

The programme includes 10 educational posts covering breastfeeding, everyday newborn care, warning signs and when to seek medical help, safe sleep, infant resuscitation, emotional adjustment to parenthood, infant development, bonding, and family and community support. Participants will also be able to send non-urgent questions about the educational content to the study researcher. This channel will not provide emergency care or replace regular healthcare services.

Participants will complete questionnaires 2-3 days after birth and again 15-17 days after birth to assess anxiety, parenting stress, and symptoms of depression. At the final assessment, they will also answer questions about their confidence in caring for their baby and their knowledge of newborn care. Those receiving the Instagram programme will additionally rate how easy it was to use.

The study hypothesis is that parents who receive the Instagram educational programme alongside usual care will report lower levels of anxiety, parenting stress, and depressive symptoms at follow-up than parents who receive usual care alone. The study will also explore whether the programme improves parents' confidence and knowledge about caring for their newborn.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) Total Score
Change from Baseline in Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) Total Score
Change from Baseline in Parental Stress Scale (PSS) Total Score
title: Anxiety Reduction, Learning Support, Mood, and Self-efficacy Adaptation in Families With Healthy Newborns

brief_summary:
Adequate nutritional support is essential in critically ill children receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. Current nutritional prescriptions are commonly based on predictive equations, which may inaccurately estimate individual energy requirements and contribute to underfeeding or overfeeding.

CALI-PED is a single-center, prospective, interventional pilot study designed to evaluate whether indirect calorimetry-guided nutritional support reduces interindividual variability in energy intake adequacy among mechanically ventilated children in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU).

Fifty children will be prospectively enrolled and compared with a historical cohort of 141 patients managed using conventional nutritional targets based on the Schofield predictive equation. In the prospective cohort, resting energy expenditure will be measured daily using indirect calorimetry, for up to seven days of invasive mechanical ventilation, and enteral caloric prescriptions will be adjusted accordingly.

The primary outcome is the interindividual variability in the ratio of actual energy intake to the reference energy target on days 2 and 3 of mechanical ventilation. Secondary outcomes include protein intake, agreement between predicted and measured energy requirements, changes in resting energy expenditure over time, duration of mechanical ventilation, PICU length of stay, and incidence of nosocomial infections.

This pilot study aims to determine whether indirect calorimetry can improve the individualization and consistency of nutritional support in critically ill children.
primary_outcomes: Interindividual Variability in Energy Intake Adequacy on Days 2 and 3 of Mechanical Ventilation
title: Indirect Calorimetry-Guided Nutritional Support in Mechanically Ventilated Children (CALI-PED)

brief_summary:
People with asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) often come to the emergency department because their breathing suddenly gets worse. These flare-ups are called exacerbations. Many of these episodes are caused by viruses or inflammation, not bacteria. However, clinicians still frequently prescribe antibiotics, even when they are unlikely to help. Unnecessary antibiotic use can cause side effects, increase healthcare costs, and contribute to antibiotic resistance, which is a growing public health problem.

The URGE study aims to find a better way to decide when antibiotics are truly needed during asthma or COPD attacks in the emergency department. The study will test whether using two rapid bedside tests can safely reduce unnecessary antibiotic prescriptions.

The first test is a rapid molecular test that looks for common respiratory viruses and certain bacteria using a nasopharyngeal swab. Results are available within about 15 to 20 minutes. The second test measures C-reactive protein (CRP) from a small blood sample. CRP is an inflammation marker that tends to be higher when a bacterial infection is present. Together, these tests give doctors quick information about whether an infection is likely viral, bacterial, or non-infectious.

URGE will recruit 200 adults who come to the emergency department with an asthma or COPD exacerbation to take part in the study. After providing consent, participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. In both groups, participants will complete both rapid tests. In one group, the test results will be shared with the treating doctor right away and can be used to help guide treatment decisions. In the other group, the doctor will not see the test results, and care will follow usual practice. Doctors will always be free to make their own clinical decisions, regardless of test results.

The main outcome the study will measure is whether or not patients are prescribed antibiotics when they leave the emergency department or are admitted to hospital. The study will also examine how long patients take antibiotics, hospital admissions, return visits to healthcare services, and patient satisfaction. Participants will be followed up by phone and through medical record review at 7 days and 30 days after their emergency visit to ensure they recover safely.

The URGE trial will study tests that are already approved and commonly used in healthcare. The goal is not to deny needed treatment, but to better match treatment to the cause of the flare-up. If successful, this approach could reduce unnecessary antibiotic use, improve patient care, and support safer, more sustainable treatment of asthma and COPD exacerbations in emergency departments.
interventions: Respiratory pathogen detection via molecular PCR
Disclosure of dual POCT results with advisory PCR+CRP algorithm
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants prescribed antibiotics at ED discharge
title: Utility of Respiratory Biomarker Guidance in Exacerbations

brief_summary:
Recovery after cardiac surgery can be challenging because patients may experience pain, breathing difficulties, reduced mobility, and delays in returning to their usual activities. Early mobilization and breathing exercises are important components of postoperative nursing care.

This study aims to determine whether a nurse-led structured mobilization and breathing exercise protocol improves the quality of recovery in patients undergoing cardiac surgery compared with routine nursing care.

The study is a single-center, assessor-blinded, parallel-group randomized controlled trial. A total of 76 adult patients undergoing elective coronary artery bypass grafting or valve replacement surgery will be included. After surgery, eligible patients who have been extubated and are clinically stable will be randomly assigned to one of two groups.

Patients in the intervention group will receive a structured program of early mobilization and breathing exercises led by nurses, in addition to routine postoperative care. Patients in the control group will receive routine postoperative nursing care.

The main outcome will be the quality of recovery measured using the Turkish version of the 15-item Quality of Recovery questionnaire (QoR-15T) at 48 hours after extubation. Additional assessments will include recovery quality at other time points, pain intensity, time to first out-of-bed mobilization, delirium, length of intensive care unit and hospital stay, and postoperative pulmonary complications.

The findings may help determine whether a structured, nurse-led approach can improve recovery following cardiac surgery.
interventions: Nurse-Led Structured Mobilization and Breathing Exercise Protocol
primary_outcomes: Quality of Recovery at 48 Hours After Extubation (QoR-15T)
title: Effects of a Nurse-Led Mobilization and Breathing Exercise Protocol on Recovery After Cardiac Surgery

brief_summary:
This observational study aims to investigate how smoking and periodontal health affect lipid profiles in saliva and blood serum. Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease that affects the tissues supporting the teeth, while smoking is an important risk factor for periodontal disease.

The study will include 56 adults divided into four groups according to their periodontal health and smoking status: non-smokers with periodontitis, smokers with periodontitis, periodontally healthy non-smokers, and periodontally healthy smokers.

Saliva and blood samples will be collected from each participant. Lipid profiles will be analyzed using liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (LC-qTOF-MS). The study will examine the individual and combined associations of periodontitis and smoking with lipid profiles and explore the relationship between lipid patterns in saliva and serum.

The findings may help identify lipid-related changes associated with periodontal disease and smoking and improve our understanding of their effects on oral and systemic health.
primary_outcomes: Salivary Lipidomic Profile
Serum Lipidomic Profile
title: The Effect of Smoking on Salivary and Serum Lipidomic Profiles in Patients With Periodontitis

brief_summary: This study evaluates a community-based physical activity programme designed to bridge the gap between hospital-based rehabilitation and independent physical activity close to home for cancer survivors. Over 12 weeks, changes in quality of life, fatigue, sleep quality, anxiety, depression and physical activity were assessed using validated questionnaires, alongside participants' motivation, expectations and satisfaction. Although no significant improvements were observed in the main health outcomes, participants reported high satisfaction and increased confidence in continuing physical activity independently. These findings highlight the potential of community-based programmes to support the transition towards long-term physical activity after cancer treatment.
primary_outcomes: Quality of Life (EORTC QLQ C-30)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether AEFIX, a new low-cost external fixation system, works as well as the external fixators currently used in Rwandan public hospitals to hold broken thigh (femur) and shin (tibia) bones in position in adults. External fixation uses metal pins placed into the bone and connected by clamps and rods outside the body. It is commonly used for severe fractures, including open fractures, that cannot safely be treated with internal plates or rods right away.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does AEFIX keep the broken bone in position as well as standard external fixators, as measured on X-rays taken after surgery and again before the fixator is removed?
* How do complications, quality of life, and fracture healing compare between the two groups?

Researchers will compare AEFIX to the external fixation systems already used as standard care at each participating hospital to see whether AEFIX is no worse than these systems at keeping the bone in place.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned, like a coin toss, to receive either AEFIX or the standard external fixator during their planned fracture surgery
* Have X-rays after surgery and before the external fixator is removed
* Return for follow-up visits about 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months after surgery, where the study team will check pin sites, healing, pain, and ability to bear weight, and ask questions about quality of life
* Receive reimbursement for transport costs to attend follow-up visits

About 150 adults will take part at up to five hospitals in Rwanda.
interventions: Standard of Care External Fixation System
primary_outcomes: Loss of Fracture Reduction
title: Assessing the Safety & Efficacy of an Affordable Fracture External Fixation System

brief_summary:
Coronary artery disease (CAD) is the leading cause of death and disability worldwide, and acute myocardial infarction (AMI, commonly known as heart attack) is its most severe and life-threatening form. In a heart attack, the time from symptoms onset to the receipt of reperfusion therapy to restore blood flow ("total ischaemic time") strongly influences how much heart muscle is saved and whether the patient survives. The longer the delay, the worse the outcome.

Despite effort to reduce in-hospital delay through establishment of chest pain centres, a critical gap remains. The time taken by patients to recognise symptoms and seek care during the prehospital stage accounts for the largest proportion of total ischaemic time. This study proposes the "Blended Eclectic Programme for Optimising Community Preparedness (BE-Prepared)" to improve timely care-seeking behaviours among CAD patients and the general public, ultimately reducing prehospital delays and improving AMI patient outcomes in Hong Kong. This programme consists of two components: a community-based health education component and a narrative intervention for CAD patients.

It is hypothesised that CAD patients who receive the BE-Prepared programme, compared with those receiving usual care, will show greater improvements in behavioural intention to seek care for AMI symptoms, better AMI knowledge, and fewer perceived barriers to care-seeking. It is further hypothesised that CAD patients who receive the programme will report a shorter onset-to-door time, be more likely to use an ambulance, and have reduced in-hospital stays and fewer 30-day major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events following an AMI episode relative to the control group.

The study uses a type 2 effectiveness-implementation hybrid design, combining a randomised controlled trial with a qualitative study to evaluate both whether the programme works and how it can be integrated into routine practice. Adults aged ≥18 with confirmed CAD but no prior AMI will be recruited from three major Hong Kong public hospitals and randomly assigned 1:1 to BE-Prepared or usual care. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, 3 months, and 12 months, with 12-month monitoring for acute coronary events, guided by the RE-AIM framework. Healthcare providers will join SWOT workshops and selected patients will be interviewed. If effective, BE-Prepared could close a critical gap in current services, reducing prehospital delay and improving AMI outcomes in Hong Kong.
interventions: Blended Eclectic programme for optimising community Preparedness (BE-Prepared)
primary_outcomes: Care-seeking attitudes and beliefs for AMI symptoms, measured by the Acute Coronary Syndrome Response Index (ACSRI)
title: Blended Eclectic Programme to Improve Community Preparedness for Acute Myocardial Infarction

brief_summary:
People with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, often continue to experience disruptions in the gut microbiome and metabolism even when their disease is in clinical remission on biologic therapy. These persistent gut-level changes may contribute to disease flares over time.

Nuts are nutrient-dense foods rich in unsaturated fats, fiber, minerals, and polyphenols, and have been shown to support gut health in general and cardiometabolic populations. However, their specific effects on the gut microbiome and metabolome in people with IBD in remission have not been examined.

This proof-of-concept study investigated whether short-term, daily consumption of a standardized mixed nut blend (almonds, walnuts, and pecans) shifts the gut microbiome and metabolic signals of people with IBD toward a healthier, control-like profile.

Sixty participants: 21 healthy controls, 19 participants with Crohn's disease in remission, and 20 participants with ulcerative colitis in remission, underwent a 3-day nut-avoidance washout, followed by 10 days of consuming 30 g/day of a mixed nut blend. Fecal samples were collected on days -3, 0, 5, and 10 and analyzed for microbiome composition (16S rRNA sequencing) and metabolite profiles (untargeted LC-MS metabolomics). Participants also completed a food frequency questionnaire and a daily adherence survey.

The study aimed to characterize how a defined, single food item influences gut health signals in IBD remission, providing a foundation for larger, longer-term dietary interventions.
primary_outcomes: Change in gut microbial composition following nut supplementation in IBD participants
Change in fecal metabolite profile following nut supplementation in IBD participants
title: Nut Supplementation in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Proof-of-Concept Study of Gut Microbiome and Metabolome Effects

Following completion of Part A, all eligible participants (including those previously on placebo) may continue into the open-label extension period (Part B) to receive radiprodil.

The placebo-controlled portion is expected to be approximately 17 weeks for participants in Part A and at least 12 months for participants in Part B.

brief_summary:
Postprandial glycemic response refers to changes in blood glucose levels following food consumption. These responses are influenced by several factors, including food composition, eating speed, and the sequence in which different food components are consumed. Rapid eating may influence glucose fluctuations, while consuming carbohydrates after other meal components, such as proteins and vegetables, may help reduce post-meal glucose spikes. However, limited research has investigated the combined effects of eating speed and meal sequencing in the context of traditional Pakistani meals.

The present study aims to investigate the effects of slow and fast eating patterns and different meal sequences on postprandial glycemic responses among young, healthy adults. The study will focus on a standardized traditional Pakistani breakfast to evaluate whether variations in eating speed and food order produce differences in post-meal blood glucose levels.

An experimental crossover study design will be used, in which participants will consume the same standardized breakfast under four different experimental conditions: (1) slow eating with carbohydrates consumed first, (2) slow eating with carbohydrates consumed last, (3) fast eating with carbohydrates consumed first, and (4) fast eating with carbohydrates consumed last. Each participant will undergo all four conditions, allowing individual comparisons of glycemic responses.

Blood samples will be collected at predefined intervals following breakfast consumption to measure postprandial blood glucose levels. The collected data will be analyzed to compare glucose fluctuations and postprandial glycemic responses across the four experimental conditions.

The study is expected to provide useful insights into the combined influence of eating speed and meal sequencing on postprandial glucose regulation. Its findings may help identify simple and practical eating strategies that support better glycemic control without requiring major changes in traditional dietary habits. Furthermore, the research may contribute to the development of culturally appropriate nutrition recommendations for the Pakistani population and provide a foundation for future studies investigating dietary behaviors and metabolic health.

Overall, this study emphasizes the importance of how quickly and in what order food is consumed, in addition to what is eaten, in influencing postprandial glycemic responses.
lead_sponsor: University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Lahore - Pakistan
primary_outcomes: Postprandial Blood Glucose Response
Postprandial Serum Insulin Response
title: Effects Of Eating Speed And Meal Order On Postprandial Glycemic Responses After A Traditional Pakistani Meal In Young Adults

brief_summary:
The REAL-LAUGH study will compare changes in body composition and other health outcomes in children and adolescents with growth hormone deficiency who start weekly or daily growth hormone treatment in routine clinical practice in Spain.

Approximately 110 participants aged 3 to 16 years will be enrolled: 55 receiving weekly long-acting growth hormone and 55 receiving daily recombinant human growth hormone. The treating physician will select treatment as part of usual care, independently of study participation. The study will not assign treatment.

Participants will be followed for 12 months, with assessments at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. The main outcome is the change in percentage total body fat measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, also called DXA, between baseline and 12 months. The study will assess whether the reduction in body fat with weekly treatment differs from that with daily treatment.

Other assessments will include lean body mass, growth, waist measurements, blood pressure, glucose and lipid metabolism, carotid artery wall thickness, bone mineral density, pubertal development, bone age, IGF-1 concentrations, and adverse events. No biological samples will be stored for research.
primary_outcomes: Change in Percentage Total Body Fat
title: Real-world Evidence With Long-Acting User-optimized Growth Hormone Therapy in Pediatric Growth Hormone Deficiency

brief_summary:
TED is an autoimmune disease that may cause stress to the corneal endothelium which may differ by the degree of inflammation.

Previous studies found that corneal endothelial cell morphology significantly changed in active TED patients compared with inactive TED patients.

The mechanism underlying the morphological changes in corneal endothelium of active TED is still unclear. One possible explanation is increased ocular surface inflammation, particularly during the active phase. Huang et al. reported elevated levels of tear inflammatory cytokines, including interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6, IL-8, and tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α in active TED compared to inactive TED and controls. Villani et al. demonstrated a higher number of activated corneal keratocytes in active TED, indicating more pronounced corneal inflammation.

Local injection of steroid has been utilized in active TED with promising results. the local steroid injection has the advantage of delivering the steroid directly to the site of the pathology maximizing its concentration and effect and minimizing the systemic side effects of steroid.

All Previous reports about corneal endothelial changes in TED were of cross-sectional design and lacks longitudinal follow-up. To the best of authors, knowledge, this is the first study to evaluate changes in corneal endothelial morphology in active TED patients following local steroid treatment.
primary_outcomes: Coefficient of Variation (CV) & Hexagonality (HEX) as percentage
title: Corneal Endothelium in Active Thyroid Eye Disease Treated With Local Steroid Injection

brief_summary: Sigh maneuver is a periodic deep breath aimed at reopening collapsed alveoli. The primary outcome was change in PaO2/FiO2 ratio; secondary outcomes included changes in PaO2, dynamic compliance, ventilatory ratio, PaCO2, and the incidence of ARDS (Berlin criteria) over one week of observation.

brief_summary:
This randomized clinical trial will compare two active doses of preservative-free intrathecal morphine (200 micrograms and 450 micrograms) for postoperative analgesia in adults undergoing major elective open urologic surgery. Participants will be assigned by chance in a 1:1 ratio to receive one of the two intrathecal morphine doses before general anesthesia. Both groups will receive the same standardized non-opioid analgesia, the same pain-assessment-guided intravenous sufentanil rescue and infusion protocol, and the same postoperative monitoring and safety measures.

The main outcome is the total amount of intravenous sufentanil administered from admission to the intensive care unit through the next 24 hours. Other outcomes include pain scores, time to first rescue sufentanil, initiation of continuous sufentanil infusion, clinically significant sedation, opioid-related respiratory depression, nausea and/or vomiting, pruritus, and clinically significant hypotension.

The study will test whether increasing the intrathecal morphine dose from 200 micrograms to 450 micrograms provides a clinically relevant additional reduction in postoperative systemic opioid requirements without an evident increase in clinically relevant adverse effects.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn how a 10-week, lower-body strength-training program changes the structure of a large thigh muscle called the vastus lateralis. Researchers want to know when these changes start, how large they are, and which processes inside the muscle cause them. They are also interested in how quickly new proteins are made in the muscle during training.

Healthy adults of any sex will take part in the study. One leg will begin training right away, and the other leg will start one week later. This staggered start lets researchers compare muscle changes at different points without taking too many muscle samples from one leg. Training sessions will be supervised and will use two common gym machines (leg press and leg extension) three times per week for 10 weeks. At the end of the program, participants will repeat the baseline tests to see how much they have improved.

Before training begins, participants will complete a series of tests, including a body-composition scan (to measure body fat and muscle mass), an ultrasound scan of the thigh muscle (to measure muscle thickness), and a strength test to find the maximum weight the leg can lift. Participants will also drink a special type of water called "heavy water." Heavy water looks and tastes like normal water but contains a form of hydrogen that lets researchers measure how fast new muscle proteins are made. The total amount of heavy water is very small. Participants drink a body-weight-based amount on the first day, split into three small doses, and then a much smaller dose every day for the rest of the study. To monitor the heavy water in their bodies, participants will provide saliva and blood samples at the beginning of the study and at each biopsy visit.

During the 10-week program participants will:

* Train three times per week on the leg press and leg extension machines under supervision.
* Drink a small amount of heavy water daily as explained above.
* Wear a Fitbit activity tracker for one week at the start, one week at the middle, and one week at the end of the study to record daily steps and sleep.
* Provide muscle samples (biopsies) from each thigh: once before and once after a workout in week 2, and once after weeks 3, 7, and 10. A brief ultrasound scan of the thigh muscle will be done at each biopsy visit to track changes in muscle thickness.

After training is completed, participants will repeat the body-composition scan, ultrasound, and strength test. The muscle samples will be analyzed in a laboratory to count the number of tiny fibres (myofibrils) inside each muscle cell, measure their size, and determine how new proteins were made using the heavy-water tracer. The researchers will also look at markers of muscle growth and repair. By comparing results from the trained and delayed legs and by looking at changes over time, the study aims to provide a detailed picture of how human muscle adapts to resistance training. This information could help health professionals design better exercise programs for building strength, preventing muscle loss, and aiding recovery from injury.
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in myofibril number per muscle fiber
Change from baseline in myofibril cross-sectional area
Change from baseline in myofibrillar area fraction
title: Investigating Subcellular Skeletal Muscle Adaptations to 10 Weeks of Lower-Body Resistance Training

brief_summary:
Heart failure is a common condition in which the heart cannot pump blood effectively. It can be caused by reduced blood supply to the heart (ischemic) or by other causes (nonischemic), and it may begin suddenly (acute) or last for a long time (chronic). Heart failure can lead to changes in the heart's structure and function, called cardiac remodeling, and to different risks of hospitalization or death.

This is a prospective, multicenter, observational study. It will enroll adults with acute or chronic heart failure, including both ischemic and nonischemic types. Participants will receive their usual medical care and will undergo multimodal assessments. These may include cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, echocardiography, electrocardiography, blood tests, and computed tomography, including high-resolution coronary CT or photon-counting CT when available. Data on heart structure, function, blood flow, tissue characteristics, and clinical outcomes will be collected during follow-up.

The main goals are to better understand cardiac remodeling in different types of heart failure and to find out whether combining information from different tests can improve risk stratification. Advanced statistical methods and artificial intelligence will be explored as part of the analysis, but artificial intelligence is not the main focus; the study aims to integrate all data sources in a balanced way. No new drug or device will be tested. The results may help doctors improve how they evaluate and monitor patients with heart failure.
primary_outcomes: Heart failure-related composite endpoint
title: Multimodal Assessment of Remodeling and Stratification in Heart Failure

brief_summary:
Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is a common condition in men, and a proportion of affected patients require surgical treatment. Transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) is considered the gold standard for the surgical management of these patients. Preoperative asymptomatic bacteriuria (ASB) is present in approximately 30% of patients with BPH undergoing TURP. Current guidelines recommend screening for and treating ASB before endoscopic urological procedures associated with mucosal trauma to prevent postoperative infectious complications. However, the precise role of ASB in the development of postoperative urinary tract infections (UTIs) remains unclear, and the quality of the evidence supporting these recommendations is low.

A prospective, comparative clinical study is therefore warranted to determine the effectiveness of preoperative screening for and treatment of ASB in preventing infectious complications in patients with BPH undergoing TURP. The findings may help address existing knowledge gaps, inform future recommendations, and promote adherence to evidence-based clinical decision-making.

The objective of this study is to determine the effectiveness of preoperative screening for and treatment of ASB in preventing postoperative infectious complications in patients with BPH undergoing TURP.

A multicenter, parallel-group, randomized non-inferiority diagnostic test trial is proposed. A total of 1,262 men aged over 45 years with a diagnosis of BPH, an indication for TURP due to BPH, and no signs or symptoms of UTI will be enrolled. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to one of two groups according to whether the results of the preoperative urine culture are disclosed or withheld. Participants will be followed up for one month, and the primary outcome will be the occurrence of urinary tract infection (UTI).

The study was approved for review by the Research Ethics Committee of the Faculty of Medicine at the University of Antioquia and by the ethics committees of all participating institutions involved in patient recruitment.
interventions: Knowledge of Preoperative Urine Culture Results
Blinding to Preoperative Urine Culture Results
primary_outcomes: Urinary tract infection (UTI)
title: Impact of Preoperative Urine Culture Following Transurethral Resection of the Prostate (UROCULTURP).

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effects of 4-7-8 breathing exercises on perceived stress, mental well-being, and quality of life in newly diagnosed patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

The study will be conducted at the Internal Medicine Outpatient Clinic of Kayseri City Hospital, Türkiye. A total of 60 patients aged 18-65 years who have been newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus and have HbA1c levels of 8% or higher will be enrolled. Participants will be randomly assigned to either the intervention group (n=30) or the control group (n=30) using simple randomization.

Participants in the intervention group will perform 4-7-8 breathing exercises twice daily, in the morning and evening, for four weeks, in addition to receiving routine diabetes treatment. The breathing technique involves inhaling through the nose for 4 seconds, holding the breath for 7 seconds, and exhaling through the mouth for 8 seconds. Participants will be instructed to perform four sets per session. Participants in the control group will continue receiving routine diabetes treatment without any additional breathing exercises.

Data will be collected at baseline and at the end of the four-week intervention using the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-14), the World Health Organization-Five Well-Being Index (WHO-5), and the Short Form-36 Health Survey (SF-36).

The study will investigate whether 4-7-8 breathing exercises improve perceived stress, mental well-being, and quality of life in newly diagnosed patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus compared with routine care alone.
primary_outcomes: Change in Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-14) Score From Baseline to Week 4
title: 4-7-8 Breathing Exercises for Stress, Well-Being, and Quality of Life in Newly Diagnosed Type 2 Diabetes

brief_summary: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurological disease that can affect movement, muscle strength, physical activity, and breathing. Individuals with MS may experience reduced physical activity and changes in pulmonary function, even during the early stages of the disease. However, the relationship between physical activity levels and pulmonary function in individuals with MS remains insufficiently understood. This observational study aims to investigate whether physical activity levels are associated with pulmonary function in adults with multiple sclerosis. A total of 94 participants with a confirmed diagnosis of MS are expected to be recruited. Physical activity will be assessed using the Arabic version of the International Physical Activity Questionnaire-Short Form (IPAQ-SF), while pulmonary function will be evaluated using spirometry. The study will examine whether individuals with different levels of physical activity also demonstrate differences in pulmonary function. The findings may help improve understanding of physical and respiratory health in individuals with MS and inform future rehabilitation assessment and management strategies.
primary_outcomes: Correlation Between Physical Activity and Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) in Individuals with Multiple Sclerosis
title: Correlation Between Physical Activity and Pulmonary Endurance in MS Patients

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the validity and reliability of the Bed Bridge Test (BBT) in adults aged 65 years and older. The BBT is a simple physical performance test that involves repeatedly lifting the hips while lying on the back.

At least 50 older adults will participate in this methodological study. Participants will complete the BBT, Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB), Timed Up and Go (TUG) Test, Barthel Index, and Katz Index of Independence in Activities of Daily Living.

Inter-rater reliability and agreement between repeated measurements performed by the same assessor during a single session will be evaluated. The relationships between BBT performance, physical function, mobility, and independence in daily activities will also be examined.

The findings may help determine whether the BBT is a useful assessment tool for evaluating physical performance in older adults.

Eligible patients will be randomly assigned to receive either sintilimab plus ipilimumab N01 and chemotherapy or sintilimab plus chemotherapy. The study aims to determine whether the addition of ipilimumab N01 to sintilimab plus chemotherapy can improve clinical outcomes in this patient population while evaluating the safety of the combination regimen.

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether adding dacarbazine to doxorubicin works better than doxorubicin alone as the first drug treatment for women with uterine leiomyosarcoma that is metastatic or has come back after surgery. A total of 100 participants will be randomly assigned to receive either doxorubicin alone or doxorubicin plus dacarbazine for up to 6 cycles of 21 days each. Researchers will compare how many participants are alive without disease progression 1 year after the start of treatment.
primary_outcomes: 1-year progression-free survival (PFS)

brief_summary:
Mental health problems among adolescents and young adults have increased globally, underscoring the urgent need for accessible, preventive, and systemic approaches to promoting student mental health. This pilot study aims to evaluate the feasibility, conversational quality, and preliminary effectiveness of an AI-powered chatbot integrated with wearable-derived physiological data intervention to provide personalized and timely mental health support for Finnish higher education students. The study explores how real-time stress indicators, such as heart rate variability (HRV), can inform the chatbot's adaptive and proactive interactions to promote students' mental health in daily life.

The study setting will be the Faculty of Medicine, University of Turku in Finland. A total of 15-20 participants will be recruited with convenience sampling for this study. The inclusion criteria for participants are: 1) enrolled students at the Faculty of Medicine, 2) voluntary and consenting, 3) Finnish-speaking, 4) having a smart phone (Android/iOS), and 5) having none to mild levels of psychological distress. Participants who self-report a diagnosis of mental health disorder, or having an acute treatment for mental health will be excluded.

The intervention in this study consists of 4-week daily use of a AI-powered chatbot. In addition to access to the chatbot, a wearable device will be given to each participant to collect physiological data related to their stress (HRV), physical activity and sleep. At the end of week 2 and 3 of the study, participants will receive a personalized report summarizing the data collected by the device. Throughout the intervention period, the research assistant will contact participants once a week to ensure their well-being. At the end of the study, an interview will be arranged with each participant.

The study data includes the conversations with the chatbot, physiological data from the wearable device, daily stress questions, background information questionnaire, Depression Anxiety Stress Scale (DASS-21) (at the beginning of the intervention and at weeks 2 and 4), Chatbot Usability Questionnaire (CUQ) (at weeks 2 and 4) and an end-of-study semi-structured interview.
interventions: AI-powered chatbot integrated with wearable-derived data
primary_outcomes: Eligibility of participants
Recruitment and retention of participants
Engagement of the participants
Technical performance of the chatbot
Safety of the chatbot
title: AI-Powered Chatbot Integrated With Wearable-Derived Data for Promoting Mental Health Among Finnish Higher Education Students

brief_summary:
Pain after open-heart surgery performed through a median sternotomy can make it difficult for patients to breathe deeply and cough, which may lead to breathing problems after surgery. The goal of this clinical trial is to compare three methods of pain control in adults having open-heart surgery: thoracic epidural analgesia, bilateral erector spinae plane block, and intravenous analgesia alone.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do thoracic epidural analgesia and erector spinae plane block lower pain scores at rest during the first 48 hours after removal of the breathing tube, compared with intravenous analgesia?
* Do these techniques improve breathing function and recovery after surgery?

Participants were randomly assigned to one of three groups. Before general anesthesia, one group received a thoracic epidural catheter with a continuous infusion of local anesthetic for 48 hours, one group received a single ultrasound-guided erector spinae plane block on both sides of the back, and one group received no regional block. All participants received the same intravenous pain medication after surgery, with additional medication if their pain score was above 4 out of 10. Pain scores, breathing exercise volumes, breathing-related complications, and length of stay were recorded.
primary_outcomes: Pain intensity at rest
title: Thoracic Epidural Analgesia Versus Erector Spinae Plane Block After Median Sternotomy

brief_summary:
Abdominal drain removal after gynecological surgery is a commonly performed procedure in female patients; however, it is often described by patients as a physically and psychologically challenging experience. During drain removal in the postoperative period, patients' pain and anxiety levels may increase.

Although pharmacological methods are effective, they may not always be sufficient on their own due to the risk of side effects and certain limitations. Therefore, it is important to investigate non-pharmacological methods and integrate them into nursing care.

This study aims to examine the effect of virtual reality glasses on pain and anxiety levels during abdominal drain removal after gynecological surgery.

The study will be conducted using a randomized controlled experimental design with parallel groups and pre-test/post-test measurements. The study sample will consist of 60 patients hospitalized in the Gynecologic Oncology Clinic of Ankara Dr. Abdurrahman Yurtaslan Oncology Training and Research Hospital. Patients will be assigned to an experimental group (n=30) or a control group (n=30).

Patients in the experimental group will watch 360-degree virtual reality videos featuring natural scenery for 10 minutes, beginning 5 minutes before abdominal drain removal. Patients in the control group will receive routine clinical care without any additional intervention.

Data will be collected using the Participant Information Form, Visual Analog Scale for Pain, State Anxiety Inventory, and Visual Analog Scale for Satisfaction.

The study is expected to contribute to improving patient comfort and integrating innovative non-pharmacological approaches into nursing care.
primary_outcomes: Change in Pain Level
Change in State Anxiety Level
Patient Satisfaction With Virtual Reality
title: The Effect of Virtual Reality Glasses on Pain and Anxiety Levels During Abdominal Drain Removal After Gynecological Surgery

brief_summary:
This clinical trial will investigate whether non-compressive therapeutic gloves improve hand function and reduce pain in people with hand osteoarthritis. The gloves contain semiconductor elements embedded in their fabric. Researchers will compare these gloves with visually identical placebo gloves that do not contain semiconductor elements.

The main question is whether the active gloves improve hand function after 12 weeks compared with placebo gloves. Researchers will also assess pain, grip strength, symptoms and changes seen on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) over nine months.

The study will involve at least 154 participants aged 39 years or older with diagnosed hand osteoarthritis who do not require immediate hand surgery. It will take place at MSK House in Sleaford, United Kingdom.

After providing written informed consent, participants will be assigned by chance to one of two groups. Each participant will have an equal chance of receiving active or placebo gloves. Neither participants nor the clinical team will know which gloves have been assigned.

Participants will:

* Wear the assigned glove or gloves on their affected hand or hands for at least 20 hours each day, including overnight, during the first 12 weeks.
* Continue wearing the gloves for at least 12 hours each day, including overnight, for the remainder of the nine-month study.
* Complete questionnaires about hand pain and function before treatment and at three, six and nine months.
* Attend the study site at the beginning and at nine months for assessments, including grip strength testing and MRI scans of the hand and wrist.
* Record their hand pain, glove use and pain medication use in a weekly diary.

Participants may also complete a short video-based movement assessment at the first and last study visits.

The main measure of hand function will be the Australian Canadian Osteoarthritis Hand Index (AUSCAN), a questionnaire about hand symptoms and difficulty with everyday activities. Other assessments will measure pain, hand function, grip strength and changes in the hand joints.

The research team will record unwanted effects during the study. Participants who experience discomfort, irritation or a skin reaction will be advised to remove the gloves and contact the study team.

The findings will help determine whether these therapeutic gloves have a role in managing hand osteoarthritis.
primary_outcomes: Change in Hand Function Assessed Using the Australian Canadian Osteoarthritis Hand Index (AUSCAN)
title: Effect of Non-Compressive Semiconductor Embedded Therapeutic Gloves on Osteoarthritis of the Hand

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate whether an artificial intelligence (AI) based software system can assist surgeons in identifying key anatomical structures during minimally invasive upper urinary tract surgery.

During these procedures, surgeons operate while viewing images from laparoscopic endoscope. Key anatomical structures, such as the kidney, renal artery and vein, ureter, renal pelvis, inferior vena cava, and left reproductive vein, as well as surgical targets such as tumors, may sometimes be difficult to distinguish because of bleeding, surgical smoke, tissue movement, changes in tissue appearance, or obstruction by surgical instruments. The study team has developed an AI-based image recognition system that analyzes surgical video in real time and identifies and outlines relevant anatomical structures on the screen during surgery.

The study has two main goals (primary endpoints):

1. To evaluate how accurately the AI system can identify and delineate key anatomical structures in surgical videos collected from different hospitals, surgeons, surgical procedures, and imaging systems.
2. To evaluate the real-time performance and technical reliability of the AI system in the operating room, including processing latency, frame rate, system failure rate, and the proportion of time during surgery in which AI-generated results are successfully displayed.

The study will include adults aged 18 years or older who undergo one of five types of minimally invasive upper urinary tract surgery: partial nephrectomy, radical nephrectomy, radical nephroureterectomy, inferior vena cava tumor thrombectomy, or pyeloplasty.

The study will be conducted at 11 hospitals in China. In the first phase, surgical videos recorded between 2015 and 2025 will be used to develop, validate, and test the AI system. In the second phase, approximately 100 patients will be prospectively enrolled from internal centers, and the AI-generated anatomical recognition results will be displayed on a monitor during surgery. Overall, approximately 1,600 retrospective surgical cases and 100 prospective cases are planned for inclusion.

The AI system is designed solely as an assistive tool for anatomical recognition. It does not make clinical decisions, provide autonomous surgical instructions, or control any surgical equipment. Surgeons remain fully responsible for all clinical and surgical decisions, and the AI display can be turned off at any time.

All participants will receive standard clinical care. Participation in the study will not involve any additional medications, surgical procedures, or blood tests. Identifying personal information will be removed from the surgical videos and clinical data used for the study, and all study data will be stored securely in accordance with applicable data protection requirements.

As secondary objectives, the study will compare the performance of the AI system with that of surgeons with different levels of surgical experience using a set of challenging surgical images or video frames. The study will also evaluate surgeons' experience with the system, including its usability, clarity of display, and whether the AI-generated information interferes with or affects the surgical workflow.
primary_outcomes: Dice coefficient
Intersection over Union, IoU
Precision
Recall
F1 score
Mean inference latency
Processing frame rate, FPS
System crash rate
title: AI-Based Anatomy Recognition in Minimally Invasive Kidney Surgery

brief_summary:
Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common and serious complication in older adults after major gastrointestinal surgery and is associated with longer hospital stay, long-term cognitive decline and higher mortality. Dexmedetomidine, a highly selective alpha-2 adrenergic agonist with sedative, anti-inflammatory and opioid-sparing effects, may reduce POD, but evidence in older patients undergoing gastrointestinal surgery remains inconsistent, and tools to identify which patients are at highest risk are lacking.

The goal of this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial is to learn whether intraoperative and early postoperative dexmedetomidine prevents POD in patients aged 60 years or older undergoing elective gastrointestinal surgery under general anesthesia, and to develop a risk prediction nomogram for POD in this population. The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does dexmedetomidine lower the incidence of POD within 5 days after surgery compared with placebo, and is it safe?
2. How accurately can a prediction model (nomogram) built from preoperative and intraoperative factors estimate each patient's risk of POD?

Researchers will also examine how dexmedetomidine changes postoperative inflammatory and stress markers (IL-6, cortisol, CRP, NLR, SII) and their association with POD, and whether the benefit of dexmedetomidine differs across baseline-risk strata.

Participants will be randomly assigned to dexmedetomidine or placebo (0.9% saline). The blinded infusion starts 15 minutes before induction of anesthesia (dexmedetomidine 0.5 mcg/kg over 15 minutes, then 0.5 mcg/kg/h until 2 hours after surgery, or the same volume and rate of saline). Delirium will be assessed three times daily with the 3D-CAM (or CAM-ICU for patients who cannot be interviewed) from the end of surgery until postoperative day 5 or hospital discharge.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of postoperative delirium
Discrimination of the postoperative delirium nomograms (C-statistic)
Calibration slope of the postoperative delirium nomograms
Calibration-in-the-large of the postoperative delirium nomograms
Brier score of the postoperative delirium nomograms
title: Dexmedetomidine for Preventing Postoperative Delirium and a Risk Prediction Nomogram in Older Adults Undergoing Gastrointestinal Surgery

brief_summary: SAMOTHRACE is a prospective, single-center, randomized controlled pilot study evaluating a home-based telemonitoring strategy in patients with advanced chronic liver disease undergoing follow-up for advanced therapies and/or liver transplantation. Participants were randomized in a 1:2 ratio to a telemonitoring intervention or standard care. The telemonitoring strategy combines home acquisition and transmission of physiological parameters with centralized clinical review and predefined alerts. Participants were followed for 12 months. The primary objective was to assess the feasibility of remote patient management, while secondary objectives included liver-related clinical outcomes, hospital readmissions, liver transplantation, and mortality.

By directly addressing the potential limitation of autonomic modulation associated with PF ablation alone, this study will provide mechanistic and clinically relevant insights into the role of parasympathetic modulation of the heart in preventing AF recurrence.

The results are expected to yield novel, clinically meaningful evidence that may help refine and optimize catheter ablation workflows, particularly in the era of non-thermal energy sources.
interventions: pulmonary vein isolation and roof line ablation
lead_sponsor: Institute for Clinical and Experimental Medicine

brief_summary: Mortality prediction in neurocritical care relies on scores computed at admission, which cannot update as the clinical course evolves. We previously developed a landmark-based machine learning model that converts hourly physiological data, including intracranial pressure, into an updating risk of death. The model was developed in a large public database and validated retrospectively in a second, independent one. This prospective multicentre study will test the model in consecutive patients at participating hospitals in Fujian Province, China. Physiological data will be collected as part of routine care. The model will generate risk estimates that are recorded for analysis but not shown to treating clinicians, and no treatment decision will be influenced by the study. The primary analysis will assess discrimination and calibration of the model for death during the intensive care stay. Secondary analyses will compare the model with severity scores in routine use and examine performance by aetiology.
interventions: Landmark machine learning mortality prediction model
primary_outcomes: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (range 0 to 1) for death during the intensive care stay at the 24-hour landmark
title: Prospective Multicentre Validation of a Landmark Machine Learning Model for ICU Mortality in Neurocritical Care

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate whether exposure to pethidine during labor is associated with breathing difficulties in late-preterm newborns. Late-preterm babies are those born between 34 weeks and 36 weeks plus 6 days of pregnancy. Although they are close to full term, they may still have an increased risk of breathing problems after birth.

The study will be conducted at two hospitals: Zagazig University Hospitals in Egypt and Royale Hayat Hospital in Kuwait. It will include approximately 320 mothers and their newborn babies.

The researchers will prospectively observe two groups of mothers receiving combined spinal-epidural (CSE) analgesia during labor. The first group will include mothers who receive pethidine in addition to CSE analgesia as part of their clinical care. The second group will include mothers who receive CSE analgesia without pethidine. The decision to administer pethidine will remain entirely with the treating medical team and will not be determined by the research study.

The main purpose is to compare the occurrence of clinically significant breathing difficulties in newborns during the first 24 hours after birth. The study will also assess the need for newborn resuscitation, oxygen therapy, respiratory support, admission to the neonatal intensive care unit, feeding difficulties, and other neonatal outcomes. Maternal outcomes will also be evaluated.

The findings may improve understanding of the association between maternal intrapartum pethidine exposure and neonatal health, particularly when pethidine is used as an adjunct during labor to facilitate cervical effacement, ripening, and dilatation alongside combined spinal-epidural analgesia. The results may help clarify the potential neonatal respiratory risks associated with this practice, support evidence-based decisions regarding intrapartum pain management and cervical preparation, and contribute to improving maternal and neonatal safety.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Clinically Significant Neonatal Respiratory Depression Within 24 Hours After Birth
title: Association Between Maternal Intrapartum Pethidine Exposure and Respiratory Depression in Late-Preterm Newborns

brief_summary:
DETECSEPS is a multicentre, randomized, open-label trial sponsored by Assistance Publique - Hôpitaux de Paris, under the scientific leadership of IHU SEPSIS - PROMETHEUS Comprehensive Sepsis Center, led by Professor Djillali Annane.

The study evaluates whether an early sepsis detection strategy combining the National Early Warning Score 2 (NEWS2) and circulating H3.1 nucleosome concentrations improves care pathways compared with usual care in adults presenting to emergency departments with suspected or confirmed infection and at least one risk factor for sepsis.

The strategy aims to support timely recognition and management of sepsis and to identify patients suitable for discharge with ambulatory follow-up when hospital admission is not otherwise indicated. The study will assess care pathway optimization at 24 hours, clinical outcomes, health-related quality of life, return to usual activities, and economic and environmental outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients with optimized care pathway

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled clinical trial is to evaluate the effects of different concentrations of etidronic acid (HEDP) combined with sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl), with or without EDDY sonic activation, on postoperative pain and 12-month clinical and radiographic outcomes in adults undergoing single-visit root canal treatment for chronic apical periodontitis.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Do different final irrigation protocols using 17% EDTA, 9% HEDP-NaOCl, or 18% HEDP-NaOCl affect postoperative pain during the first 72 hours after root canal treatment?

Does EDDY sonic activation influence postoperative pain compared with conventional syringe irrigation?

Does the effect of the final irrigation solution on postoperative pain differ according to whether EDDY activation is applied?

Do the different final irrigation protocols affect analgesic consumption during the first 72 hours after treatment?

Do these irrigation protocols influence clinical and radiographic periapical healing at 12 months, as assessed by the Periapical Index (PAI) and fractal dimension (FD) analysis?

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of six groups before root canal treatment.

Group 1: Final irrigation with 17% EDTA using conventional syringe irrigation without sonic activation.

Group 2: Final irrigation with 17% EDTA combined with EDDY sonic activation.

Group 3: Final irrigation with 9% HEDP-NaOCl using conventional syringe irrigation without sonic activation.

Group 4: Final irrigation with 9% HEDP-NaOCl combined with EDDY sonic activation.

Group 5: Final irrigation with 18% HEDP-NaOCl using conventional syringe irrigation without sonic activation.

Group 6: Final irrigation with 18% HEDP-NaOCl combined with EDDY sonic activation.

All participants will undergo single-visit root canal treatment using the same standardized endodontic treatment protocol. Root canal preparation will be performed using reciprocating nickel-titanium instruments, followed by the assigned final irrigation protocol.

In all groups, 5 mL of the assigned final irrigation solution will be applied for 60 seconds. In the sonic activation groups, the irrigation solution will be activated using the EDDY system in three consecutive 20-second cycles. In the non-activation groups, conventional syringe irrigation will be performed for 60 seconds without sonic activation.

Postoperative pain will be assessed using a 0-10 visual analog scale (VAS) at 6, 12, 24, 48, and 72 hours after treatment. The primary outcome will be the postoperative pain trajectory across these five time points, including comparisons of pain intensity between the six irrigation protocols.

Analgesic consumption during the first 72 hours will be recorded as a secondary outcome.

Clinical follow-up examinations will be performed at 3 and 6 months, followed by clinical and radiographic evaluations at 12 months. Periapical healing will be assessed by comparing baseline and 12-month PAI scores and evaluating radiographic changes using fractal dimension analysis. Clinical signs and symptoms, including spontaneous pain, percussion and palpation sensitivity, swelling, and sinus tract formation, will also be evaluated at the 12-month follow-up.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Pain Intensity Over 72 Hours
title: Effects of Etidronic Acid Concentration and EDDY Activation on Postoperative Pain and 12-Month Radiographic Outcomes in Apical Periodontitis

brief_summary: The inadequate fulfillment of national targets for COPD described above indicates that interventions designed to increase adherence to recommendations in established guidelines could improve patient outcomes. This pilot study is therefore intended to indicate if a digital educational tool can increase adherence to COPD guidelines and measurably improve measures of disease control. If the objectives of the study are met, it provides a rationale for further developing the tool and validating it in controlled studies. This is an 8-week, single-arm pilot study in patients with COPD. A total of 35 patients will be included. Based on an anticipated screening failure rate of 50%, 70 patients will be screened. Patients will receive standard of care with a board-certified physician using an educational COPD tool.
interventions: Guidance of the treating physician by a digital tool
primary_outcomes: CAT score
title: Pilot Study of an Educational Tool for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to compare the short-term effects of a protein produced through bacterial fermentation with whey protein, a milk-based protein, on blood sugar, insulin, and amino acid levels in healthy, physically active men aged 18-60 years.

The main question is whether these two protein sources produce different changes in blood sugar, insulin, and amino acid levels when consumed alone or with carbohydrate. The study will also compare the responses to protein plus carbohydrate with the response to carbohydrate alone.

Participants will consume each test drink on separate testing days after an overnight fast. Blood samples will be collected before and for three hours after each drink to measure changes over time. This study will help researchers better understand how the body responds to bacterial-derived protein compared with whey protein.
primary_outcomes: Plasma Glucose Concentrations Following Test Drink Consumption
Plasma Insulin Concentrations Following Test Drink Consumption
Plasma Free Amino Acid Concentrations Following Protein Consumption
title: Effects of Bacterial-Derived Protein and Whey Protein on Blood Sugar, Insulin, and Amino Acid Levels

brief_summary: Midwifery education requires the integration of theoretical knowledge and clinical skills to ensure effective childbirth management. However, traditional teaching methods may limit students' active participation, clinical self-efficacy, and confidence while increasing anxiety. The Jigsaw cooperative learning method is a student-centered approach that promotes active learning, peer teaching, collaboration, and clinical decision-making. Although its effectiveness in theoretical education has been demonstrated, evidence regarding its impact on childbirth-related competencies remains limited. This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effects of the Jigsaw cooperative learning method on childbirth skills self-efficacy and anxiety levels among midwifery students and to examine their opinions regarding this educational approach.
primary_outcomes: Kolb Learning Style Inventory Version III (KLSI-III)
Trait Anxiety Level (State-Trait Anxiety Inventory - STAI-II)
Childbirth Skills Self-Efficacy Scale (CSSES)
title: The Effect of the Jigsaw Cooperative Learning Method on Midwifery Students' Childbirth Skills Self-Efficacy and Anxiety
