brief_summary:
This multicenter, prospective, observational, comparative cohort study will investigate the association between atrial coronary artery involvement and newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation (AF) in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).

Patients with acute STEMI undergoing coronary angiography will be assigned to two observational cohorts according to the development of AF during the first 24 hours of hospitalization: patients with a first-ever episode of AF and patients without AF, with the latter group matched by age and sex. Coronary angiograms will be assessed for thrombosis or stenosis of the arteries supplying the atria and for their relationship to the infarct-related artery.

The primary endpoint is the incidence of atrial coronary artery involvement in patients with newly diagnosed AF during acute STEMI. Secondary endpoints include all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, acute heart failure, thromboembolic complications, major bleeding, duration of hospitalization and intensive care stay, AF recurrence, cardioversion, and prescription of direct oral anticoagulants during hospitalization.

The study plans to enroll 400 participants, with 200 patients in each cohort. The study is non-interventional, and all diagnostic and therapeutic procedures will be performed according to standard clinical care. The follow-up will include the index hospitalization and a 30-day telephone assessment.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of atrial coronary artery involvement in patients with newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation during acute STEMI
title: Atrial Coronary Circulation in STEMI Patients With Newly Diagnosed Atrial Fibrillation

The purpose of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether a combination of manual therapies, therapeutic exercises, and integrative and complementary practices reduces the loudness, discomfort, and impact of somatosensory tinnitus. This type of tinnitus is associated with changes in the neck and/or jaw joint.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Does the combined treatment reduce tinnitus loudness, discomfort, and impact more than placebo?

Are the benefits maintained three months after treatment ends?

Researchers will compare two groups: one will receive the combined treatment targeting the neck and jaw regions, and the other will receive simulated procedures (placebo) that resemble the treatment procedures.

Participants will:

Attend one session per week for 12 weeks (three months), receiving either the combined treatment or placebo, depending on the group to which they are randomly assigned.

Complete questionnaires before and at the end of the 12 weeks.

Return for a follow-up assessment three months after the sessions end to determine whether the effects have been maintained.
interventions: Manual Manipulation Without Trigger Point Deactivation

brief_summary:
The surgical management of distal radius fractures via open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) remains the gold standard for restoring wrist function. However, the procedure is traditionally characterized by repetitive workflow interruptions of the removal of metallic retractors to avoid radiological artifacts and the ergonomic strain of the "head-turn" required to view distant fluoroscopy monitors.

The Radius Radiolucent Ring Retractor (RRRR) is a single-use, 3D-printed nylon surgical device designed for hands-free retraction in arm and wrist surgeries. This device was developed at the University of Hong Kong and invention is held by HKU Versitech Limited.

This study aims to definitively evaluate the gadget-optimized distal radius fixation surgery with the RRRR and head-mounted Augmented Reality glasses display to optimize the surgical workflow. This trial will evaluate whether this system provides a more efficient alternative to conventional monitor-based fluoroscopy in modern orthopedic practice.
primary_outcomes: Total Fluoroscopy Time
Functional Assessment measured by QuickDASH Score
title: Fracture Internal X-fixation With Augmented Reality and Radiolucent Ring Retraction

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether women's satisfaction with their birth experience differs by mode of birth. It includes women aged 18 to 45 years who gave birth to a single, live, full-term baby at Ankara Bilkent City Hospital. Three groups are compared: spontaneous vaginal birth, planned cesarean section performed before labor starts, and cesarean section decided during labor (intrapartum cesarean section).

The main question it aims to answer is:

\- Do birth satisfaction scores, measured with the Turkish version of the Birth Satisfaction Scale-Revised (BSS-R), differ among these three modes of birth?

Researchers will also look at whether birth satisfaction is related to pain after birth, to how much women felt involved in decisions about how they gave birth, to personal and newborn factors, and to how many hours after birth the questionnaire was completed.

The study does not change the mode of birth or any part of routine care. Between 24 and 48 hours after birth, before going home, participants fill in a short questionnaire once (about 10 to 12 minutes). Information about labor, birth, the baby, and routinely recorded pain scores is taken from hospital records. No extra tests or procedures are done for the study.
primary_outcomes: Birth Satisfaction Scale-Revised (BSS-R) Total Score
title: Birth Satisfaction in Women After Spontaneous Vaginal Birth, Planned Cesarean, or Cesarean During Labor

brief_summary:
This observational study aims to understand how electrical activity in the brain is related to activity in the stomach, heart, respiratory system, blood pressure, and glucose levels in people with drug-resistant epilepsy undergoing stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) monitoring as part of their clinical care.

Researchers will collect synchronized recordings of brain activity and available body signals, including surface electrogastrography, electrocardiography and heart rate, abdominal respiratory movement, continuous glucose monitoring, and noninvasive blood pressure. The study will examine brain-body relationships during wakefulness, sleep, meals, seizures, and routine electrical stimulation or functional mapping performed for clinical purposes.

All decisions about SEEG implantation, electrical stimulation, functional mapping, medication, and other clinical care are made independently by the treating clinical team. The research protocol does not assign, add, or modify any electrical stimulation or treatment. The study only records and analyzes physiological responses associated with routine clinical care and naturally occurring physiological states.

brief_summary:
Hip abductor insufficiency is a challenging complication following total hip arthroplasty (THA). It may result from damage to the abductor muscles or tendons, particularly the gluteus medius and minimus, and can lead to persistent hip pain, muscle weakness, a positive Trendelenburg sign, and impaired walking ability.

Gluteus maximus transfer is a surgical procedure used to restore the function of the hip abductor mechanism in patients with severe abductor insufficiency. This study aims to evaluate the clinical and functional outcomes of gluteus maximus transfer in patients who develop abductor insufficiency following total hip arthroplasty.

The study will assess postoperative improvements in hip function, abductor strength, gait, pain, and patient-reported functional outcomes, as well as the occurrence of postoperative complications. The hypothesis is that gluteus maximus transfer can provide meaningful functional improvement in appropriately selected patients with persistent abductor insufficiency following total hip arthroplasty.
conditions: Hip Abductor Insufficiency Following Total Hip Arthroplasty
primary_outcomes: Change in Hip Abductor Muscle Strength
title: Gluteus Maximus Transfer for Hip Abductor Insufficiency Following Total Hip Arthroplasty

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether the drilling technique used to prepare the implant site affects the experience and satisfaction of adult patients receiving dental implants. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do patients treated with under-drilling report a different experience, satisfaction and postoperative discomfort than patients treated with conventional drilling?
* How are implant insertion torque, implant stability and bone density related to the pain and experience reported by patients?

Researchers will compare under-drilling (the implant site is prepared with a slightly narrower final drill than usual) with conventional drilling (the standard drilling sequence for the implant diameter). Both are standard clinical techniques.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of the two techniques, without knowing which one they receive
* Have their dental implant(s) placed at the CEU Cardenal Herrera University Dental Clinic
* Complete a questionnaire about their experience before surgery and immediately after surgery
* Record their experience every day during the first week after surgery
* Complete a quality-of-life questionnaire (OHIP-14) one week after surgery
primary_outcomes: Patient Experience and Satisfaction (Visual Analogue Scale)
title: Patient Experience Across Dental Implant Drilling Protocols

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare two urine testing methods used to diagnose urinary tract infections (UTIs) in adults aged 60 years and older.

The main question this trial aims to answer is:

Does Guidance® UTI testing, compared with standard urine culture, improve patient outcomes and help healthcare providers make more appropriate antibiotic treatment decisions?

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to either Guidance UTI testing or standard urine culture testing.
* Provide a urine sample during their initial clinic visit.
* Complete questionnaires at the initial visit and approximately 14 and 28 days later.

Researchers will compare UTI-related repeat medical visits, emergency care, hospitalizations, new UTI diagnoses, and antibiotic treatment decisions between the two groups.
primary_outcomes: Percent difference between diagnostic test arm in the number of composite negative outcomes
title: Standard Culture Versus Advanced Guidance UTI® Testing in Older Adults

brief_summary:
Background With population aging accelerating worldwide, age-related hearing loss (ARHL) has become one of the most prevalent sensory impairments among older adults, with global prevalence rising from 12.7% at age 60 to over 58% by age 90. The communication difficulties, reduction in daily-life activities, and social stigma associated with hearing loss can contribute to increased loneliness in older adults. This condition affects approximately 25% of older adults in mainland China and 46% in Hong Kong and is associated with depression, increased mortality risk, and elevated healthcare utilization. Addressing loneliness in this population is therefore essential not only for older adults' own health and wellbeing, but also for promoting healthy aging and sustainable community-based care. However, limited studies have examined the associations between loneliness and physical, psychosocial, and hearing health status among older adults with ARHL in real-life living environments and no qualitative study has explored their perceptions and experiences of loneliness. The built environment may influence both hearing health and loneliness among older adults by shaping communication opportunities, social participation, mobility, and access to supportive resources. Therefore, examining the relationships among loneliness, hearing difficulties, and the built environment is important for understanding how everyday living contexts contribute to or mitigate loneliness in later life. Furthermore, existing intervention studies have concentrated mainly on hearing aids and cochlear implants. However, loneliness in this population arises not only from reduced auditory input, but also from psychological distress, social exclusion, and limited opportunities for social engagement, all of which are factors that hearing correction alone cannot directly resolve. These gaps limit the evidence base needed to understand and address loneliness in this population and hinder the development of multi-component interventions for older adults with ARHL.

Aim This study aims 1) to explore the perceptions and experiences of loneliness and social engagement among older adults with ARHL; 2) to examine the associations between loneliness and physical, psychosocial, hearing health, and built environment factors; and 3) to develop and preliminarily evaluate a Multidomain Approach through Biopsychosocial Pathways (MAP) intervention to address loneliness in this population.

Methods A sequential exploratory mixed methods design was adopted, underpinned by the Socio-Ecological Model. This study will be conducted in three phases. First, a qualitative descriptive methodology was used among community-dwelling older adults with ARHL to explore their perceptions and experiences of loneliness and social engagement. Second, a cross-sectional study, with GIS-based spatial analysis will be conducted to examine the associations between loneliness and physical, psychosocial, hearing health, and built-environment factors. Last, a pilot randomized controlled trial will be conducted to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary effects of MAP, underpinned by the biopsychosocial model and findings of previous phases to reduce loneliness among older adults with ARHL.

Expected outcomes This study is expected to 1) provide in-depth qualitative evidence on the perceptions and experiences of loneliness and social engagement among older adults with ARHL; 2) identify multilevel correlates of loneliness, spanning physical, psychosocial, hearing health, and built environment factors; 3) evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary effects of MAP on loneliness, thereby informing the design of a future definitive trial and community-based service planning for this population.
interventions: Multidomain Approach through Biopsychosocial Pathways (MAP) intervention
primary_outcomes: Adherence to the three intervention components
Usage Frequency to the three intervention components
Participant retention rate
The follow-up assessment completion rate
Acceptability of the intervention assessed by semi-structured interviews
title: Multidomain Approach Through Biopsychosocial Pathways (MAP) Intervention for Older Adults With Age-Related Hearing Loss

brief_summary:
This study aims to find out whether changing the wording and content of workplace emails can encourage more healthcare and non-healthcare staff to get a seasonal flu vaccine. The main question is whether emails that highlight the benefits of vaccination, the possible consequences of not getting vaccinated, or vaccination rates among colleagues are more effective than standard information emails.

The study will take place during the 2026-2027 flu vaccination campaign across 17 healthcare and social care organizations in Lombardy, Italy. Approximately 45,000 eligible workers are expected to be included, covering both staff who provide patient care and those in administrative, technical, and support roles.

Workplace groups, such as departments or organizational units, are randomly assigned to one of four email communication approaches:

* Standard information (control): emails communicating that the vaccination campaign is ongoing and that it is possible to get vaccinated.
* Benefits of vaccination (gain framing): emails emphasizing the potential benefits of vaccination for workers, patients, colleagues, and the organization.
* Consequences of not getting vaccinated (loss framing): emails emphasizing the possible risks and negative consequences for workers, patients, colleagues, and the organization.
* Vaccination among colleagues (social norms): emails and follow-up updates showing vaccination progress and, where possible, comparing vaccination rates in the recipient's workplace group with those in other groups.

Researchers will use existing vaccination and employment records to compare the percentage of workers who receive a flu vaccine in each group by the end of the campaign. They will also examine whether the emails encourage earlier vaccination and whether their effects differ across workplaces and staff groups. Where suitable records are available, they will explore differences in sickness absence during the campaign.

Vaccination will remain voluntary, and all workers will continue to have access to the usual vaccination services. The study involves workplace emails and the use of existing records; no additional medical visits, tests, or procedures are required.

The findings will help healthcare organizations decide whether simple changes to routine communication can improve staff flu vaccination rates and which approach works best.
primary_outcomes: Influenza vaccination uptake at the end of 2026-2027 campaign.
title: Increasing Flu Vaccination Through Evidence-Based Nudges

brief_summary:
This study aims to test a 6-week nature-based program called "Forest for Mothers" to help women with mild-to-moderate postpartum depression (PPD). PPD is common, but current treatments can be hard to access or may not be safe for breastfeeding mothers. We are testing whether spending time in nature in a group setting can improve mood and well-being.

We will recruit 40 mothers who gave birth within the last 3 years and have mild-to-moderate depressive symptoms. Participants will be randomly assigned to either a forest therapy group or a standard care group. The forest therapy group will attend weekly 2-hour guided sessions in an urban forest park for 6 weeks. These sessions include gentle walking, sensory exercises, meditation, group sharing, and nature-based creative activities. The standard care group will receive an information booklet on postpartum depression management.

All participants will complete questionnaires about their mood, stress, sleep, and quality of life at the start of the study, after 6 weeks, and at 3- and 6-month follow-ups. We hope to find that this nature-based program is an effective, accessible, and safe non-drug option to help mothers feel better.
primary_outcomes: Change in Depressive Symptoms (EPDS Score)
title: Can Spending Time in Nature Help Mothers With Depression After Childbirth? A 6-Week Forest Therapy Study

brief_summary:
Heart failure is a chronic illness with a high prevalence and impact on the quality of life of the people who experience it, associated with high hospital taxes and mortality. Beyond the results of traditional clinics, factors such as health literacy, therapeutic adherence and self-healing play a key role in the evolution of this pathology. Various studies show that inadequate health literacy levels lead to better control of malaria, more re-entry and a lower quality of life.

The objective of this research is to evaluate the effectiveness of a standard health education care program, led by nurses specialized in heart failure, initiating discharge from hospitals and with structured follow-up during the first few months afterward, compared to conventional care. It is intended to analyze its impact on health literacy, therapeutic adherence, self-healing, and quality of life, as well as explore the associated social determinants.

It will last a random clinical trial between two groups (intervention and control) at the Heart Failure Unit of the Figueres Hospital. The participants will be adults admitted for decompensation of heart failure and will be followed for 12 months, with evaluations at admission, at 6 months and at any time after discharge. It is important to serve validated instruments to measure quality of life, health literacy and therapeutic adherence.

It is hoped that the intervention will improve the quality of life and health literacy of people with heart failure, contributing to more equitable care, centered on the person and oriented towards better health outcomes.
interventions: Visit with specialist nurse with structured interview, application of scales and educational intervention
primary_outcomes: Number of patients with nursing intervention who need hospital admission in a year
Number of visits to the emergency room in the past year for patients who have undergone the nursing intervention
title: Effectiveness of a Standardized Healthcare Education Program in People With Heart Failure

brief_summary: This multicenter, cross-sectional observational study aims to characterize olfactory function in patients with sinonasal diseases and investigate its associations with disease severity, clinical characteristics, and inflammatory markers. Olfactory function will be assessed using the MultiScent-20 digital odor identification test. Additional assessments will include sinonasal symptom severity, quality of life, endoscopic and radiological findings, and clinical and laboratory markers suggestive of type 2 inflammation. Healthy volunteers without olfactory complaints will serve as a comparison group. The study is expected to enroll 3,800 participants across participating centers in Brazil.
primary_outcomes: MultiScent-20 odor identification score
title: Olfactory Function in Patients With Sinonasal Diseases: A Multicenter Observational Study

brief_summary:
Dental anxiety is common in children and can affect their behavior and cooperation during dental treatment. However, it is not fully understood how children's dental anxiety is related to their body's biological stress response.

The aim of this observational study is to investigate the relationship between dental anxiety, salivary stress biomarkers, and children's behavior during restorative dental treatment.

Children aged 6 to 10 years who require restorative dental treatment with local anesthesia will be invited to participate. Dental fear will be assessed using the Children's Fear Survey Schedule-Dental Subscale (CFSS-DS), and anxiety at different stages of the appointment will be assessed using a facial rating scale. Children's behavior during treatment will be evaluated using the Frankl Behavior Rating Scale.

Three saliva samples will be collected: before treatment, immediately after treatment, and approximately 20-30 minutes after treatment. These samples will be used to measure cortisol and alpha-amylase, two biological markers associated with the stress response.

The study will examine whether children with higher levels of dental anxiety show different biological stress responses or behavioral patterns during dental treatment. The findings may help improve the assessment and management of dental anxiety in pediatric dental care.

All dental treatments will be provided according to routine clinical needs. Participation in the study will not determine the type of dental treatment received.
primary_outcomes: Change in Salivary Cortisol Concentration
Change in Salivary Alpha-Amylase Activity
title: Dental Anxiety and Stress Response During Dental Treatment in Children

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a high-resolution computed tomography scan (HR-pQCT) can detect and describe calcium crystal deposits in the hands and wrists of adults with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How often does the HR-pQCT scan detect calcium crystal deposits in the hand and wrist joints of people with RA?
* Can the HR-pQCT scan find calcium deposits that standard tests (x-rays and ultrasound) miss? Researchers will compare scan results from participants with RA to results from participants with known calcium pyrophosphate deposition (CPPD) and participants without joint inflammation.

During a single clinic visit, participants will:

* Have standard x-rays of their hands and wrists
* Have a routine ultrasound of their hands and wrists
* Have an HR-pQCT scan of their wrist and finger joints, which takes about 15 to 20 minutes and uses a very low dose of radiation
interventions: High-Resolution peripheral Quantitative Computed Tomography Imaging
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of CPPD-suggestive calcium deposits on HR-pQCT in rheumatoid arthritis
title: Added Value of HR-pQCT in Detecting Calcium Deposits in Rheumatoid Arthritis

brief_summary:
Elevated blood levels of vitamin B12 are sometimes discovered unexpectedly during routine blood tests. Persistently elevated vitamin B12 levels can occur for several reasons, including liver disease, kidney disease, blood disorders, vitamin B12 supplementation, and certain solid cancers. However, a high vitamin B12 level alone does not indicate whether cancer is present, and it remains unclear which patients should undergo further investigations.

The KB12 study aims to determine whether measuring specific blood markers involved in vitamin B12 transport and uptake can help distinguish elevated vitamin B12 levels associated with solid cancers from those related to other conditions. Researchers hypothesize that these markers may differ according to the underlying cause of the elevated vitamin B12.

In this multicenter study, participants with persistently elevated vitamin B12 levels will provide a blood sample for laboratory analysis. Researchers will compare the levels of these markers between participants with solid cancers and those with other identified causes of elevated vitamin B12. Participants will also be contacted by telephone approximately one year later to check for any newly diagnosed conditions. Participation will not change their usual medical care.

The results may help develop more targeted approaches to investigating persistently elevated vitamin B12 levels, with the long-term goal of improving early cancer detection while avoiding unnecessary examinations.
primary_outcomes: Between-group differences in vitamin B12-related biomarker concentrations
title: Persistent Vitamin B12 Hypervitaminemia: Identification of Biomarkers for the Early Detection of Solid Cancers

brief_summary:
Post-stroke oropharyngeal dysphagia is a common complication of stroke that may impair swallowing-related motor function and increase the risk of associated complications. Although conventional swallowing exercises are widely used in rehabilitation, the immediate effects of proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF) compared with conventional swallowing exercises remain unclear.

This randomized controlled trial will aim to compare the immediate effects of a single session of PNF and conventional swallowing exercises on laryngeal elevation, cervical and temporomandibular joint range of motion, muscle strength, and perceived general well-being in individuals with post-stroke oropharyngeal dysphagia.

A total of 31 participants with fiberoptic endoscopic evaluation of swallowing-confirmed oropharyngeal dysphagia will be randomly assigned to either the PNF group or the conventional swallowing exercise group. Each participant will receive one supervised intervention session lasting approximately 50 minutes. Outcome measurements will be performed immediately before and after the intervention.

The study will investigate whether PNF produces different immediate changes in swallowing-associated and head-neck motor function compared with conventional swallowing exercises.
primary_outcomes: Change in Laryngeal Elevation
title: Immediate Effects of PNF and Conventional Swallowing Exercises in Post-Stroke Dysphagia

brief_summary:
Developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) is a condition in which a baby's hip joint does not develop normally. Ultrasound is commonly used to assess the hips of young infants for DDH, but these examinations usually require trained ultrasound staff and specialist interpretation.

The purpose of this study is to determine whether a handheld ultrasound device combined with artificial intelligence (AI) can be used by non-specialist health care personnel to obtain and assess ultrasound images of infant hips. Infants attending the Baby Hip Clinic at The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids) will undergo their usual clinical ultrasound as part of their standard care. They will also have an additional research ultrasound performed using the handheld device.

Researchers will compare the research ultrasound with the standard clinical ultrasound. The study will assess the quality of the images obtained using the handheld device and compare the AI-assisted assessment with the diagnosis from the standard ultrasound and assessments made by experienced reviewers. The research ultrasound and AI results will not be used to make treatment decisions for participating infants.
interventions: Handheld Point-of-Care Hip Ultrasound with AI-Assisted Analysis
primary_outcomes: Agreement in Alpha Angle Measurements
title: Assessment of AI-Assisted Ultrasound in DDH

brief_summary:
This study will test whether adding niacin, a form of vitamin B3, and selenium, a mineral, to standard treatment improves organ function in adults with septic shock. It will also assess the safety of this combination.

The study plans to enroll 148 patients aged 19 years or older in the emergency intensive care unit at Seoul National University Hospital in South Korea. Participants will be assigned by chance to one of two groups, with an equal chance of receiving either niacin plus selenium or placebo infusions. The placebo infusions use saline and glucose (sugar) solutions and do not contain the study drugs. All participants will receive standard treatment for septic shock.

Study treatments will be given through a vein twice a day during the first week of hospitalization. Participants and the researchers assessing outcomes will not know which treatment each participant receives. The study pharmacist and a designated team that prepares and gives the infusions will know the treatment assignments.

The main comparison will be organ function on the seventh day of hospitalization, measured using the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score. This score measures how well several organs are working. Researchers will also compare survival at 28 and 90 days, time spent in intensive care, and time on a breathing machine. Blood samples will be collected at enrollment, approximately 72 hours later, and on study day 7 to measure niacin and selenium levels and biomarkers related to antioxidant activity and oxidative stress. Possible side effects will be monitored through daily assessments and blood tests.
primary_outcomes: Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) Score on Hospital Day 7
title: Niacin and Selenium Combination Therapy in Patients With Septic Shock

brief_summary:
* Objective:\*\* This study was designed to evaluate the effects of mindfulness-based psychoeducation on psychological resilience and insight among individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia.
* Methods:\*\* This randomized controlled study with a pretest-posttest control group design was conducted at a Community Mental Health Center between January and December 2025. The study included 66 individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia, with 32 participants allocated to the intervention group and 34 to the control group. Participants in the intervention group received a structured mindfulness-based psychoeducation program consisting of one preparatory session and eight group-based sessions, whereas participants in the control group did not receive this intervention. Both groups continued to receive routine psychiatric care. Data were collected using the Descriptive Characteristics Form, the Brief Resilience Scale (BRS), and the Birchwood Insight Scale (BIS). Psychological resilience and insight were assessed before and after the intervention to evaluate potential changes associated with mindfulness-based psychoeducation.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Brief Resilience Scale (BRS) Total Score
title: The Effect of Mindfulness-Based Psychoeducation on Psychological Resilience and Insight in Individuals Diagnosed With Schizophrenia

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy of AxoGuard HA+ (hyaluronic acid nerve protector) in preventing Frey syndrome following parotidectomy. A parotidectomy is a surgical procedure to remove all or part of the parotid gland, the largest salivary gland located near the ear and jaw. The specific aims are to determine whether placement of AxoGuard HA+ during parotidectomy can significantly reduce both clinical and subclinical incidence of Frey syndrome compared to standard surgical technique alone.
primary_outcomes: Number of subjects with positive Starch-Iodine test
title: Hyaluronic Acid Barrier in Parotidectomy

brief_summary:
Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is the most prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder in child and adolescent psychiatry, affecting approximately 8% of the population worldwide. Beyond the inattention, hyperactivity and impulsivity that define it in DSM-5, ADHD is consistently associated with attentional and executive deficits considered central to its symptomatology. Its aetiopathogenesis is multifactorial and remains poorly understood: decades of research have identified no specific genetic or environmental factor.

The gut microbiota modulates the bidirectional gut-brain axis, notably through the intestinal mucosa, which secretes neuromediators such as serotonin and precursors of dopamine implicated in concentration and in ADHD. Roughly ten case-control studies have reported differences in gut microbiota diversity, richness and composition between individuals with ADHD and typically developing individuals, and several have associated specific bacterial taxa with symptom severity. Methodological heterogeneity across these studies has so far precluded consensus on a specific bacterial signature. Critically, they relied almost exclusively on clinical questionnaires, which are subjective and vulnerable to respondent and observation bias, and did not assess the cognitive deficits that characterise the disorder. To date, no study has investigated the relationship between gut microbiota composition and cognitive performance measured with standardised neuropsychological tests in children with ADHD compared with typically developing children. This is the specific gap addressed here.

This monocentric, prospective, case-control observational study will enrol 140 French-speaking children aged 6 to 12 years: 70 children with ADHD, combined presentation, diagnosed according to DSM-5 criteria and recruited from the paediatric psychiatry clinics of the Hôpital Universitaire de Bruxelles (Erasme and HUDERF sites), and 70 typically developing children recruited through advertisements. Children are excluded for prematurity, IQ below 75, psychiatric or serious chronic disease, gastrointestinal or inflammatory bowel conditions, coeliac disease, food intolerances, eating disorders, dietary supplements within 4 weeks, and antibiotics, proton pump inhibitors or any psychotropic medication within 3 months, yielding a medication-free ADHD sample and removing major confounders of microbiota composition.

Each participant attends a single assessment visit. A stool sample is self-collected at home the day before or the day of the visit using a stabilising collection kit, then stored at -80 °C. Metagenomic DNA is extracted, the V1-V3 region of the 16S rRNA gene is amplified with universal eubacterial primers, amplicons are sequenced on an Illumina MiSeq platform, and reads are processed with the QIIME2 pipeline, in academic collaboration with the Louvain Drug Research Institute (UCLouvain). At the same visit, participants complete a cognitive assessment comprising the WISC-V (estimated IQ), selected subtests of the Test of Attentional Performance (visual and auditory selective attention, divided attention, vigilance, flexibility, Go/NoGo inhibition, working memory) and the Maudsley Index of Delay Aversion. ADHD symptom frequency and severity are rated by the physician using the ADHD Rating Scale IV, and dietary habits are documented with a Food Frequency Questionnaire completed before the visit.

The study has three objectives: to determine whether gut microbiota composition and diversity differ between children with ADHD and typically developing children, and to identify a possible imbalance or bacterial signature; to compare attentional and executive performance between the two groups and examine its association with microbiota composition; and to explore correlations between the severity of inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms and microbiota composition. The hypotheses are that children with ADHD differ from typically developing children in microbiota diversity and composition, that they show poorer attentional and executive performance associated with their microbiota composition, and that their microbiota is associated with clinically rated symptom severity.

primary_outcomes: ADHD-RS IV
Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ)
IQ Test

The Maudsley Index of Delay Aversion

The goal of this randomized crossover clinical trial is to determine whether acute or subacute nitrate supplementation with concentrated beetroot juice improves submaximal exercise performance in elite athletes. The optimal nitrate supplementation regimen using concentrated beetroot juice has not yet been clearly established. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does subacute nitrate supplementation, consisting of seven days of twice-daily Beet It Sport consumption followed by an additional dose on the morning of testing, improve submaximal exercise performance compared with acute nitrate supplementation alone?
* Does subacute nitrate supplementation result in greater improvements in submaximal oxygen consumption (VO₂), time to exhaustion, and physiological responses during exercise than acute nitrate supplementation?

Researchers will compare the two nitrate supplementation regimens in the same athletes to determine which approach provides the greatest improvement in submaximal exercise performance. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups, each completing both supplementation regimens in a different order, with a 2-4-week washout period between interventions to minimize potential carryover effects.

Participants will:

* Complete the recruitment and informed consent process.
* Attend three study visits, including an initial VO₂ max assessment and subsequent exercise testing visits.
* Complete both supplementation regimens in a randomized crossover design:
* Subacute nitrate supplementation: Consume 70 mL of Beet It Sport twice daily for seven days before the exercise test, followed by 140 mL on the morning of the test.
* Acute nitrate supplementation: Consume 70 mL of placebo twice daily for seven days before the exercise test, followed by 140 mL of Beet It Sport on the morning of the test.
* Undergo exercise testing, including submaximal VO₂ assessment and a time-to-exhaustion test, as well as measurements of vital signs and capillary blood lactate levels.
* Complete a questionnaire assessing adherence to the assigned supplementation regimen.

No additional follow-up will be required after the study visits. The findings may help establish the most effective nitrate supplementation regimen using concentrated beetroot juice to optimize submaximal exercise performance in elite athletes.
primary_outcomes: Submaximal exercise test
title: Evaluation of Chronic and Acute Beetroot Juice Supplementation on Submaximal VO2 in High-Level Athletes

brief_summary:
Breast cancer remains the most prevalent malignancy among women worldwide, with a continuously increasing incidence. As a crucial component of comprehensive cancer treatment, radiotherapy plays a key role in reducing local recurrence rates and improving overall survival outcomes. However, traditional radiotherapy target volume contouring and treatment planning design rely heavily on clinician expertise, presenting challenges such as prolonged processing time, significant inter-observer variability, and high subjectivity in dose optimization. Although artificial intelligence has made substantial progress in automated contouring and planning, conventional single-modal models still face major limitations. These models struggle to effectively integrate clinical text, tumor biological characteristics, and dose distribution factors, resulting in restricted generalizability. Therefore, developing an intelligent radiotherapy assistance system capable of multimodal data fusion is of high clinical significance to enhance precision and efficiency in breast cancer radiotherapy.

This study aims to develop an innovative breast cancer radiotherapy assistance system based on a multimodal large language model. By integrating multimodal imaging data (including CT, MRI, and ultrasound), pathology reports, and structured electronic health record text, the system realizes end-to-end intelligence from target volume contouring to treatment plan generation. Employing a multicenter, ambidirectional cohort design, the study collects comprehensive clinical data from breast cancer patients who have undergone breast-conserving surgery or mastectomy. Technologically, the system innovatively combines the natural language processing capabilities of large language models with the image analysis strengths of deep learning, utilizing attention mechanisms to achieve deep fusion and interactive comprehension of heterogeneous medical data. Notably, the system breaks through traditional radiotherapy planning workflows by jointly optimizing target contouring and dose planning as a unified pipeline, applying reinforcement learning algorithms to dynamically balance target volume coverage with organ-at-risk protection. The outcomes of this study will provide an important paradigm for the clinical application of AI in radiation oncology and advance the field of precision radiotherapy.
interventions: Multimodal LLM-assisted target volume auto-segmentation and intelligent radiotherapy planning system
primary_outcomes: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of Target Volume Auto-Segmentation
title: Multimodal LLM for Breast Cancer Radiotherapy Target Auto-Contouring and Planning

brief_summary:
Preterm birth represents a major challenge in pediatric healthcare, as preterm infants are at increased risk of neonatal complications and long-term neurodevelopmental impairments. Several factors may contribute to these outcomes, including gestational age at birth, postnatal comorbidities, and the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) environment. Furthermore, preterm birth and prolonged hospitalization may negatively affect maternal psychological well-being, increasing the risk of stress, anxiety, and depression. These conditions may influence maternal sensitivity and responsiveness, mother-infant interactions, and infant neurodevelopment.

Emerging evidence suggests that maternal mental health may affect infant neurodevelopment through both direct biological mechanisms, such as epigenetic regulation, and indirect pathways, including changes in breast milk composition. Cortisol, a stress-related hormone present in breast milk and saliva, may play a role in stress regulation and neurobehavioral development. In particular, the methylation of Long Interspersed Nuclear Element-1 (LINE-1 or L1), a mobile genetic element involved in genomic regulation, may be influenced by environmental factors and early maternal care. Preliminary findings indicate that preterm infants exhibit lower L1 promoter methylation levels at birth than term infants, while early maternal care may modulate these levels and support neurobehavioral development.

The EMBRACE study aims primarily to investigate the relationship between biological maternal stress, measured through salivary cortisol levels, and L1 promoter methylation in blood samples collected from preterm infants from birth to 12 months of corrected age. Secondary objectives include examining this relationship in buccal swab samples, assessing associations between maternal perceived stress, anxiety, and depression and infant L1 methylation, and investigating the relationship between maternal psychological and biological stress indicators and infant neurodevelopmental outcomes. The study will also explore associations between perceived maternal stress and cortisol concentrations in breast milk and saliva, as well as longitudinal changes in L1 methylation.

This is a non-pharmacological, observational cohort study conducted at the Neonatology and Neonatal Intensive Care Unit of the Fondazione IRCCS Ca' Granda Ospedale Maggiore Policlinico in Milan, Italy. Participants will include preterm infants born between 24+0 and 30+6 weeks of gestational age and their mothers. Assessments will be conducted at five time points: birth, transition to intermediate care or 34 weeks of postmenstrual age, hospital discharge, 6 months, and 12 months of corrected age. Maternal assessments will include standardized questionnaires evaluating stress, anxiety, and depression, as well as cortisol measurements in saliva and breast milk. Infant assessments will include L1 methylation analyses in blood and buccal samples and standardized neurodevelopmental evaluations as part of routine clinical follow-up. No additional invasive procedures will be performed, as blood samples will be collected during routine clinical care.

The study is expected to improve understanding of the relationships between maternal stress, anxiety, depression, epigenetic regulation, and neurodevelopment in preterm infants. It will also investigate the potential role of breast milk cortisol in these associations. Ultimately, the findings may contribute to the development of early interventions aimed at improving neurodevelopmental outcomes in preterm infants and supporting maternal psychological well-being.
lead_sponsor: Fondazione IRCCS Ca' Granda, Ospedale Maggiore Policlinico
primary_outcomes: Epigenetic changes on LINE1 (blood samples)
Maternal salivary cortisol
title: Exploring the Interplay Between Maternal Stress, Human Milk, and Epigenetic Changes in Preterm Infant's Neurodevelopment

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized clinical trial is to determine whether adding recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rtPA), a clot-dissolving medicine, to gas injection and anti-VEGF treatment improves outcomes in people with submacular hemorrhage (SMH) caused by polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy (PCV).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does adding rtPA increase the proportion of participants with complete displacement of blood from beneath the fovea, the center of the macula, at 1 week after treatment?
* Does adding rtPA improve vision at 6 months and reduce complications, particularly vitreous hemorrhage (bleeding into the gel inside the eye) within 1 month after treatment?

Researchers will compare two pneumatic displacement (PD) strategies: anti-VEGF treatment plus C3F8 gas and rtPA (triple PD) and anti-VEGF treatment plus C3F8 gas without rtPA (dual PD). This comparison will assess the additional benefits and risks of rtPA. The study will enroll 80 participants at a single center. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of the two groups, with an equal chance of receiving either treatment.

The primary outcome is complete SMH displacement at 1 week, defined as no remaining blood beneath the fovea on optical coherence tomography (OCT), a scan that produces detailed images of the retina. Secondary outcomes include changes in best-corrected vision at 6 months, vitreous hemorrhage within 1 month, retinal detachment and other serious complications during follow-up, and the number of anti-VEGF injections over 6 months.

Participants will:

* Undergo baseline eye examinations, vision testing, and retinal imaging.
* Receive injections of anti-VEGF medicine and C3F8 gas into the affected eye, with or without rtPA, according to their assigned group.
* Follow the prescribed face-down positioning instructions for 3 days after treatment.
* Attend follow-up visits at 1 week and at 1, 3, and 6 months after treatment for vision testing, eye examinations, and retinal imaging, and receive further anti-VEGF treatment as needed.
lead_sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University, School of Medicine
primary_outcomes: Rate of complete SMH displacement at 1 week after the procedure.
title: Pneumatic Displacement With Anti-VEGF and Concomitant rtPA for PCV-related Submacular Hemorrhage

brief_summary:
Carotid artery stenosis is a common cause of ischemic stroke in the U.S. and disproportionately affects older adults. Patients with carotid artery stenosis face a complex set of decisions when choosing a treatment strategy. Patients must choose among surveillance with medical therapy alone, versus medical therapy plus one of three different procedures. Each treatment option has different levels of evidence to support it, some of which are decades old. Each procedural option has different expected periprocedural courses, different recoveries, and different cardiovascular risks. This challenging decision is amplified among older adults, where decisional values are often different from younger patients traditionally studied in randomized or observational studies. A decision aid could assist patients and providers who are navigating this decision, but no decision aid currently exists that includes all the contemporary carotid artery stenosis treatment options. In addition, as of October 2023, participation in a shared decision-making conversation is a Medicare-mandated component of carotid stenosis care, with reimbursement for procedures predicated on the documentation of the conversation with the patient.

The objective of this project is to conduct a single arm open label trial to test the feasibility of using a paper-based decision aid for patients considering carotid revascularization. The investigators will conduct a feasibility trial using the decision aid on older adults who are considering carotid revascularization. The investigators will recruit 50 participants aged 65 or older from the vascular surgery clinic and administer the decision aid. The investigators will purposively sample at least 10 participants that are age 80 or older. Primary outcomes will center on feasibility, and secondary outcomes will center on decisional conflict and regret.
primary_outcomes: Time to administer the decision aid
Understanding of the decision aid
title: Carotid Decision Making

brief_summary:
Acute cholangitis is an infection of the bile ducts, usually caused by a blockage that prevents bile from flowing normally. It can lead to serious complications if not treated promptly. Treatment generally includes antibiotics and drainage of the blocked bile duct, usually through a procedure called endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP).

Although antibiotics are essential for treating acute cholangitis, the optimal duration of antibiotic treatment after successful bile duct drainage remains uncertain. Current guidelines generally recommend 4 to 7 days of antibiotic treatment. However, shorter treatment may be sufficient after the source of infection has been effectively controlled, potentially reducing unnecessary antibiotic exposure, side effects, hospital stay, and healthcare costs.

The purpose of this study is to determine whether a shorter course of antibiotic treatment (4 days) is as effective as the standard course (7 days) in patients with moderate to severe acute cholangitis who have undergone successful bile duct drainage.

This is a multicenter, randomized, open-label study involving adults aged 19 years or older with moderate to severe acute cholangitis. Patients whose bile duct obstruction has been successfully relieved by ERCP within one day of hospital admission and who meet the study eligibility criteria may participate. Eligible patients will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to one of two treatment groups.

The short-course group will receive antibiotics for a total of 4 days, while the standard-course group will receive antibiotics for a total of 7 days. In both groups, intravenous antibiotics will initially be given for at least 2 days. Patients who are clinically stable and able to take oral medication will be switched to oral antibiotics as early as possible. Antibiotic selection may be adjusted according to bacterial culture results and antibiotic susceptibility testing. If the initial antibiotics are found to be ineffective, or if the patient's clinical condition requires additional treatment, the antibiotics may be changed or extended to ensure patient safety.

The primary outcome is the clinical cure rate within 14 days after randomization. Cure will be assessed based on the resolution of infection-related symptoms and improvement in blood bilirubin levels, defined as a reduction of at least 50% from the initial level or normalization, without predefined treatment failure events.

Secondary outcomes include recurrence of cholangitis between days 14 and 30 among patients who initially achieve clinical cure, all-cause mortality within 30 days, total duration of antibiotic use, and patient-reported health status and satisfaction with treatment. The incidence of adverse events within 14 days will also be evaluated. Additional assessments will compare hospital stay and total treatment costs between the two groups.

Participants will be followed up at approximately 14 and 30 days after randomization to assess treatment outcomes, recurrence of infection, additional antibiotic use, and safety.

This study aims to provide evidence on whether a 4-day antibiotic treatment strategy, combined with early conversion from intravenous to oral antibiotics after successful bile duct drainage, can achieve comparable treatment outcomes to the standard 7-day regimen. The findings may help establish a more appropriate antibiotic treatment strategy for patients with acute cholangitis while reducing unnecessary antibiotic exposure and its associated burden.
primary_outcomes: the clinical cure rate within 14 days after randomization
title: Duration of Antibiotic Therapy Evaluation Study in Acute Cholangitis (DATES-AC): An Open-Label, Multicenter, Randomized Non-Inferiority Trial Comparing Short-Course Versus Standard-Course Antibiotic Therapy After ERCP With Early Intravenous-to-oral Switch in Patients With Acute Cholangitis

brief_summary: Healthcare workers report significantly worse mental health and wellbeing than the average employed Canadian. Evidence suggests that healthcare workers' leisure-time physical activity is associated with higher mental and physical health, while occupational physical activity is not. Our pilot work demonstrated that previously inactive healthcare workers who develop sustained off-site, at-home exercise routines using mobile applications (apps) have improved depressive symptoms and burnout, and lower rates of sick leave. Yet, in our work, only 23% of healthcare workers remained engaged with the apps for at least 80 or more minutes on average per week at the end of the 12-week study. In semi-structured interviews completed following their participation in the study, healthcare workers voiced their desire to have support from our team to help them maintain their motivation and improve their adherence. Here, we propose to conduct a randomized trial with two conditions of an aerobic exercise mobile app (using a suite of apps for whole body weight-based training, yoga, pilates, and barre) with or without support from a qualified exercise professional trained in motivational interviewing to improve healthcare workers' engagement with the suite of apps in their leisure time. In turn, we aim to improve their mental health and wellbeing as their exercise levels increase. By targeting adherence, our goal is to develop a feasible, engaging, and accessible solution that can be implemented as a more widely utilized program in the future, for healthcare workers and beyond.
primary_outcomes: Exercise Engagement
title: Remote Exercise iNtErvention for Wellbeing (RENEW) Trial

brief_summary:
This study investigated whether adding cognitive-motor dual-task training to regular basketball practice could improve basketball-specific performance in male adolescent players. Cognitive-motor dual-task training involves performing basketball movements while simultaneously completing cognitive tasks that require attention and information processing.

Thirty male basketball players aged 15-17 years were randomly assigned to an experimental group (n = 15) or a control group (n = 15). Both groups continued their regular basketball training. The experimental group additionally completed a two-week cognitive-motor dual-task training program consisting of 12 sessions, conducted six days per week for approximately 20 minutes per session.

Basketball-specific performance was assessed before and after the intervention using two-point shooting, passing, and dribbling/change-of-direction tests. Each performance measure was evaluated under both single-task and dual-task conditions.

The study aimed to determine whether additional cognitive-motor dual-task training produced greater improvements in basketball-specific performance than regular basketball training alone, particularly when players performed motor and cognitive tasks simultaneously.

brief_summary:
Gum treatment (non-surgical periodontal therapy, also called scaling and root planing) reduces swelling in the gums. As the swelling goes down, the gum tissue around the teeth can shrink. This change is hard to measure with routine dental examinations. This study uses a 3D intraoral scanner, which takes digital images of the mouth without X-rays, to measure how much the gum tissue of the upper jaw changes in volume after treatment.

The study also asks whether this change is different in people with type 2 diabetes compared with people without diabetes. Diabetes can slow healing and change the body's inflammatory response, but its effect on gum volume after periodontal treatment has not been measured in three dimensions before.

Adults with stage III periodontitis who attend the Periodontology clinic at Afyonkarahisar Health Sciences University, Faculty of Dentistry, are invited to take part. Participants receive their routine gum treatment, which is not changed because of the study. Their upper jaw is scanned with an intraoral scanner before treatment and again at the routine 3-month check-up. The two scans are overlaid on a computer, and the change in gum volume is calculated. Researchers then compare people with and without type 2 diabetes.

Diabetes status and HbA1c values are taken from existing health records. The study does not require extra blood tests, X-rays, or extra visits.
primary_outcomes: Change in Buccal Marginal Gingival Soft Tissue Volume of the Maxilla
title: Intraoral Scanner Assessment of Maxillary Marginal Soft Tissue Volume Change After Non-Surgical Periodontal Therapy in Type 2 Diabetes

brief_summary:
This study explores how two simulation-based educational approaches support junior doctors in making clinical decisions when information is uncertain or incomplete. Both groups attend a one-day course with teaching on adaptive expertise and practice in simulated clinical scenarios.

The intervention group works with reflective cases, uses observation sheets focused on adaptive expert behaviour, and takes part in debriefing guided by the Behavioral Framework for Adaptive Expert Performance (BAEP). The comparison group receives instructor-led case teaching, uses open observation sheets that may draw on scenario learning objectives, and takes part in TeamGAINS debriefing.

Two course days are held each semester, with 16 participants per day. Within each semester, one day is randomly allocated to each approach. Participants are not informed whether their course day is assigned to the intervention or comparison group.

The study examines adaptive behaviour in simulation, participants' experiences discussed during debriefing, and changes in general self-efficacy and reactions to uncertainty. The qualitative BAEP analysis includes simulation recordings from the first four course days in autumn 2026 and spring 2027, with approximately 64 participants. Questionnaire and debriefing data are collected across eight course days, provisionally through spring 2028, with an anticipated total of 128 participants. Questionnaires are completed before and immediately after the course and three months later. The study compares the complete educational approaches rather than the isolated effect of any single component.
interventions: Reflective cases and BAEP-guided observation and debriefing
primary_outcomes: Adaptive expert behavior in simulated clinical scenarios

brief_summary:
Primary Objective: To describe the changes in macular fluid within 12 months in patients with neovascular agerelated macular degeneration (nAMD) complicated by pigment epithelial detachment (PED) receiving 8mg aflibercept treatandextend (T\&E) therapy.Secondary Objectives:(1) To explore the correlation between changes in macular fluid (e.g., fluctuation index \[FI\], volume change, etc.) and visual acuity improvement;(2) To evaluate the associations of macular fluid changes (e.g., fluctuation index \[FI\], volume change, etc.) and different types of fluid components with alterations in retinal and choroidal structures (e.g., disruption of the ellipsoid zone, thickness of each retinal layer, choroidal thickness, microstructural parameters on OCT and OCTA, etc.);(3) To assess the safety of 8mg aflibercept injections in nAMD patients with PED (e.g., incidence rates of retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) tear, elevated intraocular pressure, endophthalmitis and thromboembolic events).

1. Study Design (1) Type: Prospective, single-arm, open-label, multicenter study. (2) Sample size: The sample size was calculated based on the Fluid Index (FI) with reference to the results of the TOWER study. The TOWER study described the 24-month macular fluid fluctuation after intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy (bevacizumab, ranibizumab and 2 mg aflibercept) for nAMD in the real-world setting. This study hypothesizes that 8 mg aflibercept is non-inferior to the above three agents in controlling fluid fluctuation. Based on the TOWER study, the assumed mean FI at Month 12 is 42.9 with an SD of 9.8; a sample size of 38 yields a two-sided 95% confidence interval with a half-width of 3.22. Assuming a 20% dropout rate, the minimum number of patients required to reach the primary endpoint is 48. (3) Rationale for indication: The study population consists of patients with nAMD, for which aflibercept is a first-line treatment. The intervention is intravitreal injection of 8 mg aflibercept, whose efficacy and safety have been demonstrated in previous Phase III clinical trials. The T\&E regimen is a globally recognized optimized treatment strategy that reduces the treatment burden on patients and healthcare facilities while maintaining sustained disease control.
2. Study Procedures This study includes a 3-week screening period to assess subject eligibility, followed by a 48-week treatment period. Subjects who provide consent, meet all inclusion criteria and do not meet any exclusion criteria will receive intravitreal injection of 8 mg aflibercept in the study eye. Referencing the ALTAIR study, this study adopts the T\&E (treat-and-extend) regimen: one intravitreal injection is administered at Week 0, Week 4 and Week 8 during the loading phase, and the maintenance phase starts at Week 20. During the maintenance phase, all decisions to extend, maintain or shorten the dosing interval are made according to the T\&E criteria. The treatment interval should be shortened if any of the following occurs: new fluid (across all tomographic scans), no improvement or worsening of pre-existing fluid, a loss of ≥5 letters in visual acuity compared with the last visit, an increase of ≥100 μm in CRT in the central 1 mm subfield relative to the previous minimum value, or new neovascularization / new submacular hemorrhage. If the criteria for interval shortening are not met, the current interval will be maintained if fluid persists but shows a continuous decreasing trend; the injection interval may be extended as appropriate if there is no active fluid on OCT. In principle, the injection interval is adjusted within the range of 8-24 weeks, with a default adjustment step of 4 weeks each time.
primary_outcomes: Fluctuation Index
title: Observation on the Efficacy of Aflibercept 8mg Intravitreal Injection Solution on Retinal Fluid in nAMD Patients With PED

brief_summary:
This Study will be performed with fifteen (15) Heart Failure (HF) patients for remote monitoring of health and medication adherence following hospital discharges. Participants will be enrolled into two groups: Group 1 (chronic) will be enrolled on Day 30 to 180 post hospital discharge and monitored for 30 days; Group 2 (Acute) will be enrolled on Day 1-3 of hospital discharge after recent HF episodes and monitored for 30 days. Each participant will receive a Pill Dispenser being developed by the study sponsor, a BP machine, a weighing scale and a smartphone loaded with the software developed by the study sponsor that can collect and summarize participant's health data for study physician's/nurse's evaluation. Both BP machine and weighing scale record participant's data automatically to send to the study team physician/nurse for evaluation of his/her health. Outpatient pharmacy will deliver 30 days (+7) of medications as prescribed by the patient's physician in the standard pharmacy vials, and the patients will procure them from their chosen pharmacy outlet. Prescription details for medications will also be sent to the participant's mobile phone.

Medications will be uploaded in the dispenser on Day 1 by the patient in presence of a visiting nurse (a member of the study team) who will review and explain medication records with the patient. Nurse will also review and set up the machine as necessary for the daily wellness parameters to be measured and entered by the patient. Data will be collected automatically for the length of the study (30 days).

A 24-hr telephone number will be available to each patient to contact study nurse for any issues related to medication dispensing and/or health.

Devices will be returned to the study investigator on Day 30 and the remaining pills in the pill dispenser will be manually counted by the study nurse in both groups for comparing against the automatically collected data.

brief_summary:
This multicenter, prospective, single-group, pre-post pilot study aims to evaluate the preliminary effectiveness, feasibility, and acceptability of an eight-week Compassion Cultivation Training (CCT) program among healthcare professionals working in intensive care units in Córdoba, Spain.

The study adopts a quantitative-dominant mixed-methods approach, combining longitudinal quantitative assessments with a complementary qualitative evaluation of participants' experiences. Approximately 50 healthcare professionals from Hospital Universitario Reina Sofía and Hospital Cruz Roja de Córdoba are expected to participate.

The intervention consists of a structured, non-pharmacological, psychoeducational compassion training program delivered by a certified CCT instructor. The eight-session program combines six synchronous online sessions with two final in-person integrative sessions. It incorporates mindfulness practices, self-compassion training, compassion toward others, emotional regulation, reflective exercises, and practical applications to healthcare settings.

The primary objective is to assess changes in professional compassionate capacity from baseline to postintervention, measured using the Capacity for Compassion Scale developed for healthcare professionals. Secondary objectives include evaluating changes in self-compassion, compassion toward others, compassion satisfaction, burnout, compassion fatigue, psychological distress, resilience, and job satisfaction.

Quantitative assessments will be conducted at baseline (T0), immediately after the intervention (T1), and approximately three months after program completion (T2). Feasibility and acceptability will be assessed through recruitment, attendance, adherence, program completion, questionnaire response rates, and participant satisfaction.

Additionally, a complementary qualitative evaluation will be conducted at postintervention through five open-ended questions exploring participants' perceived benefits and useful practices, application of compassion-related skills in intensive care, perceived changes in workplace relationships, difficulties or adverse experiences associated with the training, and suggestions for improvement. Responses will undergo descriptive thematic analysis and will be considered alongside quantitative findings to provide additional insight into intervention feasibility, acceptability, and perceived applicability.

Given the exploratory nature of this uncontrolled pilot study, findings will be interpreted as preliminary intervention-associated changes rather than evidence of definitive causal effectiveness. The results will inform the feasibility and methodological design of future controlled studies targeting healthcare professionals working in intensive care settings.
primary_outcomes: Change in Professional Compassionate Capacity From Baseline to Postintervention
title: Compassion Cultivation Training in Intensive Care Healthcare Professionals: A Multicenter Pilot Study

brief_summary: Colorectal cancer is the third most common type of cancer worldwide and can be fatal if not diagnosed early. This study examines two different methods used to inform individuals aged 50-70 about colorectal cancer screening: traditional health education and a counseling approach known as "motivational interviewing." Motivational interviewing helps individuals feel more confident and willing to undergo screening by encouraging them to talk about their concerns and guiding them toward making positive decisions. The aim of the study is to determine which method is more effective in improving individuals' health-related beliefs and attitudes regarding colorectal cancer, as well as their actual participation in screening programs. The findings will help us enhance the support we provide to individuals in safeguarding their health.

This study aims to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of a novel virtual reality (VR)-based cognitive-motor rehabilitation program for individuals with traumatic brain injury (TBI). The intervention uses the Virtual Reality Color Trails Test (VR-CTT), which combines cognitive tasks with upper-limb movements in an immersive virtual environment.

The study consists of two stages. The first stage is a feasibility pilot involving 15 participants who will complete three VR training sessions over one week. The second stage is a randomized controlled trial involving 80 participants allocated to either VR-CTT training combined with standard rehabilitation or a control group receiving standard rehabilitation with additional therapy time. The intervention will consist of nine sessions over three weeks.

The study will assess feasibility, safety, executive functions, upper-limb motor performance, balance, and functional outcomes.

Brief Summary Carotid endarterectomy performed under regional anaesthesia allows the awake patient to be examined during carotid cross-clamping, so that a shunt is inserted only when a neurological deficit appears. A superficial cervical plexus block alone does not reliably anaesthetise the carotid sheath, whereas a deep cervical plexus block carries a risk of phrenic nerve palsy and neuraxial spread. Adding an ultrasound-guided carotid sheath block may avoid both problems.

This retrospective cohort study reviews the records of consecutive adults who underwent elective carotid endarterectomy under combined ultrasound-guided superficial cervical plexus block and carotid sheath block at Bach Mai Hospital, Hanoi, between February 2025 and February 2026. The main question is whether the combined block allows the operation to be completed under regional anaesthesia. The study also examines whether the number of patent collateral pathways of the circle of Willis on routine preoperative computed tomography angiography is associated with the need for an intraluminal shunt.
interventions: Ultrasound-guided superficial cervical plexus block combined with carotid sheath block
primary_outcomes: Completion of carotid endarterectomy under regional anaesthesia
title: Combined Superficial Cervical Plexus and Carotid Sheath Block for Awake Carotid Endarterectomy

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to examine how a brief, classroom-based kindness intervention affects students' and teachers' well-being and classroom ecology. The main questions this study aims to answer are:

1. Does participation in the kindness intervention improve teachers' psychological well-being, social and emotional competence, classroom-related functioning, and physiological stress regulation?
2. Does participation in the kindness intervention improve students' psychological well-being, social and emotional competence, classroom functioning, and physiological stress regulation?
3. Does the kindness intervention positively influence classroom ecology (e.g., classroom climate, relationships, and prosocial interactions)?
4. Does the kindness intervention produce contagion effects within classrooms (i.e., does kindness spread from teachers to students and among peers)?

Researchers will compare an active control group with two experimental groups: one in which only teachers participate in the kindness intervention and another in which both teachers and students participate independently in the kindness intervention. These comparisons will examine whether implementing the kindness intervention with both teachers and students produces greater improvements in well-being and classroom ecology than implementing the intervention with teachers alone or participating in an active control condition.

Participants assigned to the kindness intervention will be asked to perform three distinct acts of kindness toward others on one day per week for four weeks. Participants assigned to the active control group will be asked to count their daily activities on one day per week for four weeks.

The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a digital decision support tool integrated within an electronic medical record system, with or without training and mentorship for health workers, can reduce unnecessary antibiotic prescribing in patients of all ages (children and adults) who visit primary healthcare clinics in Zanzibar, Tanzania with an acute infectious illness. The main question it aims to answer is:

• Does the proportion of patients who are prescribed an antibiotic go down at clinics using these approaches, compared with clinics providing usual care?

Researchers will compare three groups of clinics to see if the approaches lead to fewer antibiotics being prescribed:

* Digital decision support and dashboard: a tool built into the Zanzibar Electronic Medical Record system (ZanEMR) that guides health workers during consultations, together with a dashboard comparing the antibiotic prescription from that clinic to other clinics.
* Digital decision support and dashboard, plus training and mentorship: the same tool, together with "Antibiotic Stewardship Club" meetings that build knowledge, encourage helpful attitudes and allow health workers to learn from one another
* Usual care: clinics continue to work as normal Whole clinics, rather than individual patients, are assigned by chance to one of the three groups. Participating clinics are public dispensaries or health centers that treat sick children and adults and have ZanEMR in their consultation rooms.

Participants will:

* Visit a participating clinic as usual for an acute infectious illness
* Receive care from health workers who are using the digital tool, taking part in the stewardship club meetings, or providing usual care, depending on their clinic's group
* Be called seven days after their visit by the research team, to record their health status
lead_sponsor: Center for Primary Care and Public Health (Unisante), University of Lausanne, Switzerland
primary_outcomes: Systemic antibiotic prescription
title: Digital Antibiotic Stewardship and Training for Wahudumu wa Afya (DAWA) Project
